articles.title: Lamine, favorito al Balón de Oro en 2027
articles.standfirst: Para 1XBET es el principal candidato a llevarse el galardón el año que viene
articles.summary: Para 1XBET es el principal candidato a llevarse el galardón el año que viene
articles.body: El Balón de Oro 2026 acaba de entregarse en Londres y ya hay cuotas para el de 2027. Harry Kane se llevó el galardón por primera vez, por delante de Kylian Mbappé y Lamine Yamal. Sin embargo, el mercado de las casas de apuestas no se detiene y ya ha fijado quiénes son los candidatos para la próxima edición, con un nombre claro en lo más alto. El favorito de las apuestas deportivas es Lamine Yamal, con una cuota de 4.5 en 1XBET. El jugador del Barcelona ha sido segundo en 2025, por detrás de Dembélé, y tercero en 2026, lo que demuestra una regularidad que ningún otro aspirante puede igualar a su edad. Con apenas 19 años, ya firma temporadas que otros necesitan una década para construir, y el mercado entiende que su techo todavía está lejos. Además, el Barça arrancó esta campaña con una racha de nueve victorias seguidas en Liga antes de caer en el Clásico, un escenario en el que su estrella tendrá visibilidad todo el año. Muy cerca aparece Kylian Mbappé, a cuota 5.5. El delantero del Real Madrid fue segundo este año y es, por números, el aspirante más constante en los últimos ejercicios, aunque sigue sin levantar el premio individual más importante del fútbol. Su cuota refleja que el mercado lo ve como el rival más serio de Yamal, pero también que su techo se mide por títulos colectivos. Un Madrid más fuerte en Europa le daría el impulso que le falta. Jude Bellingham ocupa el tercer puesto del mercado, a cuota 11. El inglés tiene el potencial de un centrocampista capaz de decidir partidos grandes. Es la apuesta de quien cree que la esta temporada será la de su explosión definitiva, con un Madrid que necesita de su mejor versión para pelear por todo. Harry Kane cotiza a 12 en 1XBET, un precio llamativo para el reciente ganador. Su temporada fue extraordinaria: Bota de Oro, máximo goleador mundial, Bundesliga, Copa de Alemania, Supercopa y semifinales de Champions con el Bayern. A sus 33 años, repetir exige igualar unas cifras difíciles de mantener, y el mercado lo tiene en cuenta, aunque mantiene su nombre por la sencilla razón de que sigue siendo uno de los mejores definidores del planeta. A la misma cuota de 12 aparece Michael Olise, su compañero en el Bayern. El extremo francés cerró 2026 en el noveno puesto y vive una evolución constante, con un papel cada vez más importante en el equipo bávaro. Si el Bayern vuelve a ser protagonista en Europa, su candidatura crecerá, y el mercado ya lo sitúa por delante de nombres con más pedigrí. Erling Haaland comparte esa cuota de 12. El noruego del Manchester City fue octavo y sigue siendo la máquina de goles más temida de Europa. Su techo es indiscutible, pero su historia con este premio es la de un delantero que suma números sin llegar a convencer a los votantes, que suelen primar los títulos colectivos. Su precio refleja esa mezcla de potencial y duda. Por detrás, a cuota 17, aparece Vinícius Júnior. El brasileño no estuvo entre los diez primeros este año, y su aspiración depende de recuperar el nivel que le llevó a ser el favorito en 2024. Si el Madrid triunfa y él es decisivo, el premio de esa cuota puede resultar muy atractivo. Cierra la lista Ousmane Dembélé, también a 17. Ganó el premio en 2025 y este año fue séptimo, en una campaña en la que el PSG repitió título de Champions League. Su perfil, dependiente del rendimiento del equipo, hace que su cuota sea la de un jugador que puede volver a la pelea si París vuelve a dominar Europa.

articles.title: Fresh representation seeks update on complaints against Odisha Gymnastics Association
articles.summary: KOLKATA: A fresh representation has been submitted to Odisha Sports Department seeking an action-taken report on complaints filed against Odisha
articles.body: KOLKATA: A fresh representation has been submitted to Odisha Sports Department seeking an action-taken report on complaints filed against Odisha Gymnastics Association (OGA) earlier this year. The latest letter, which is in possession of TOI, received by the department on October 28, seeks details on whether any inquiry or verification has been conducted and what action has been taken so far on the allegations.The original complaint had questioned the sanction of Rs 1.96 crore and release of Rs 98 lakh by the state govt to OGA for conducting the National Gymnastics Championships.It alleged governance irregularities, non-conduct of elections for several years, lack of transparency, alleged age-fraud cover-ups and financial irregularities within the association. The complaint had also raised concerns over the continued use of the name of late OGA president Samir Dey in official correspondence submitted to authorities.Questions were also raised over the association’s compliance with National Sports Code, its recognition status and utilisation of public funds released for the event.Sources told TOI that the complaints were subsequently referred to Odisha Olympic Association (OOA), which was asked to constitute a committee to examine the allegations. While the status of the committee’s findings could not be immediately ascertained, the latest representation seeks an update on the progress of the probe and any action taken by the authorities.Notably, when contacted by TOI following the original complaint, OGA general secretary Ashok Sahoo, whose signature appeared on the invoice submitted to Sports & Youth Services Department, had admitted that the use of the deceased president’s name in official documents was an oversight.In his fresh representation, complainant Balunkeswar Sahoo urged the department to disclose the action taken on the earlier complaint. “This matter concerns public interest and the proper utilisation of govt resources and therefore requires urgent and transparent action,” the representation stated.The sports department is yet to officially comment on the latest representation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mirabai Chanu pulls out of World Championships with back issue; Gyaneshwari Yadav finishes eighth
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while
articles.body: Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue.Gyaneshwari, 23, from Chhattisgarh, recorded a combined lift of 198kg, with 88kg in the snatch and 110kg in the clean and jerk, to finish on top of Group C. Her total was also better than those achieved by several lifters from Groups A and B.The Asian Championship silver medallist could have improved on her personal best of 199kg and secured a higher overall finish had she converted two missed attempts, one in each section.Chanu, meanwhile, was forced to pull out before making her much-anticipated debut in the 53kg category. She had been assigned to Group B with an entry total of 200kg but withdrew after experiencing back pain.China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg (98kg+123kg). American Eleanor Ulrey took silver with 220kg (98kg+122kg), while North Korea's So Hyon Kim secured bronze with 214kg (91kg+123kg).The snatch competition also saw seven lifters register lifts of at least 90kg, a benchmark Chanu has been working towards for more than six years.At the World Championships, lifters are divided into groups based on their declared entry totals, which represent the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk. Group A features those with the highest entry totals, followed by Groups B, C and D.The World Championships is among six events in the first phase of the qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PODCAST: Vikings’ 6–0 Start Meets Its Next Test: Kyler Murray, Brian Flores and the Lions
articles.summary: Minnesota’s undefeated streak faces a fierce divisional clash in Detroit. Analyze third-down efficiency, Blake Cashman’s defensive command, and the keys to s...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's last unbeaten team, but their next challenge could reveal plenty about their championship potential. In this episode, Halk breaks down Minnesota's 16–10 victory over Indianapolis and previews a divisional trip to Detroit.

Kyler Murray's explosive scramble helped change Sunday's game, but can the offense become more consistent without relying on spectacular individual moments? Halk examines third-down struggles, early-down execution and why finishing possessions with touchdowns remains essential as the schedule becomes more demanding.

Blake Cashman takes center stage following his NFC Defensive Player of the Week performance. Beyond the tackles, sacks and passes defended, discover how his communication helps connect Brian Flores' defensive vision to what happens on the field. The episode also celebrates Harrison Smith's milestone interception and explains why veteran recognition and discipline matter in decisive situations.

Offensively, Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson remain central to Minnesota's next step. Halk discusses how smarter opportunities, connected route concepts and purposeful aggression can help Murray maximize his receiving options.

Get an initial injury report breakdown involving Aaron Jones, Joe Huber and Brian O'Neill, plus Detroit developments worth monitoring before kickoff. Then, explore three priorities for beating the Lions: forcing difficult downs, handling road communication and giving the defense more offensive support.

Finally, Skol Court tackles the debate surrounding Minnesota's undefeated record, followed by a schedule look ahead featuring Buffalo, Green Bay, San Francisco and Atlanta.

Expect confident opinions, relatable humor and clear football explanations that help Vikings fans enjoy the wins while recognizing what comes next.

articles.title: Kings beat Senators 6-5 in OT after blowing a 4-goal lead in the 3rd period
articles.summary: LOS ANGLES (AP) — Quinton Byfield scored at 3:37 of overtime and the Los Angeles Kings beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 on Thursday night after blowing a four-go...
articles.body:
LOS ANGLES (AP) — Quinton Byfield scored at 3:37 of overtime and the Los Angeles Kings beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 on Thursday night after blowing a four-goal lead in the third period.

Byfield beat goalie Samuel Ersson with a snap shot from the high slot, with Drew Doughty picking up his third assist of the night on the play.

Erik Haula tied it for Los Angeles on a first-period power play and Trevor Moore, Mikey Anderson, Joel Armia and Artemi Panarin scored in the second to make it 5-1. Panarin capped the run on a power play after Ottawa's Hayden Hodgson was tossed for boarding defenseman Brandt Clarke.

Clarke missed the rest of the game because of an upper-body injury.

Ottawa roared back in the third, with Shane Pinto tying it at 5 with 1:40 left and Ersson off for an extra attacker.

Dylan Cozens scored twice in the period and Drake Batherson also connected. Cozens and Batherson struck in a 33-second span, and Cozens cut it to a goal with 7:26 remaining. Tyler Kleven opened the scoring for Ottawa in the first period.

Darcy Kuemper made 17 saves for Los Angeles.

Jonas Johansson stopped 12 of 16 shots before giving way to Ersson in the second. Ersson made 20 saves on 22 shots.

articles.title: Why Drone Delayed Panthers-Packers TNF Game
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers were driving and faced a third-and-1 inside the 10-yard line. The Carolina Panthers already trailed 20-10 and were trying to prevent it...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers were driving and faced a third-and-1 inside the 10-yard line.

The Carolina Panthers already trailed 20-10 and were trying to prevent it from getting too much worse.

The play-by-play announcer, Al Michaels said, "We've got a drone, not ours."

The NFL couldn't continue the game while there was an unidentified drone in the area.

The officials sent the players to their sidelines.

The game was delayed for about five minutes.

The Amazon broadcast eventually informed the viewing audience that the drone had departed and that everything was good to proceed.

It appears the Packers put together a good plan during the drone delay.

On the first play afterward, Jordan Love threw to Josh Jacobs for a short touchdown.

The Trey Smack extra point made it a 27-10 Packers lead with 7:30 left in the third quarter.

On the one hand, it's a lot of time for the Panthers to make up the deficit.

The Packers got even more good news during the delay.

Their star wide receiver Christian Watson had left the game in the first half and been taken to a local hospital for evaluation for a chest injury.

But evidently just about when the drone delay was happening, the ambulance was pulling back into Lambeau Field.

The Amazon broadcast showed Watson hustling out of the ambulance to find the locker room and get back out onto the field.

Green Bay may not even need him, but it's not good news for the Panthers, either — whose cornerback Will Lee III appears to have gotten the worst side of the collision with Watson in the first half.

articles.title: Who was Jilieta Gallego? Spanish long jumper among 69 killed in train collision
articles.summary: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego, 24, was among those killed in a train collision in Toledo province that claimed at least 69 lives.
articles.body: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego, 24, was among those killed in a train collision in Toledo province that claimed at least 69 lives. The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation (RFEA) expressed its condolences following her death on Thursday."The Spanish athletics family joins in the grief over the passing of Julieta Gallego, athlete of AD Sprint, in the train accident that occurred in Urda (Toledo)," the federation said in a statement on X, offering its support to her family, friends and teammates at the club.Gallego represented Madrid-based AD Sprint and regularly competed in Spain's club championships. She recorded a personal best of 5.90 metres (19 feet 4 inches) in the long jump at Antequera in 2023."There are blows that strike at the very heart of the athletics family. Today, the sport mourns the passing of Julieta, a life ahead of her that has been unjustly extinguished," RFEA president Raul Chapado told Spanish newspaper ABC.Two high-speed trains collided on Wednesday in the second deadly accident in less than a year on the railway line connecting Madrid to the southern region of Andalusia.Former Spanish minister Fátima Báñez also died following Wednesday's collision. She served as minister for employment and social security between 2011 and 2018. Her death was confirmed by the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE), which she chairs.Rescue teams are continuing to search for survivors among the wreckage. The crash also left more than 100 people injured.A total of 544 people were travelling on the two trains when they collided between the towns of Mora and Orgaz, near Toledo. articles.title: Everton beat Newcastle to set up League Cup quarterfinal with Fleetwood
articles.summary: Holders Man City will take on Bradford City, Crystal Palace will welcome Sunderland, while Bournemouth play Liverpool.
articles.body:
Everton advanced to the League Cup quarterfinals with a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United, setting up a clash against fourth-tier side Fleetwood Town.

First-half goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney put the hosts in control before Thierno Barry struck after the break at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, with Dan Burn scoring late for the visitors on Thursday.

The Merseyside club eased through despite the absence of midfielder Jack Grealish, who was dropped from the squad following an internal breach of club discipline. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, an Everton supporter, was among the crowd.

Everton will travel to League Two side Fleetwood, who stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth-round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.

Crystal Palace will welcome Sunderland, while Bournemouth will play away at Liverpool, who beat Chelsea 6-5 in a dramatic penalty shootout on Wednesday.

Defending champions Manchester City will take on third-tier side Bradford City. They avoided the fate that befell Arsenal and stayed on course to retain their title by twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 against Brighton , then triumph 4-3 in the shootout.

The quarterfinals are scheduled to take place in the week beginning December 14.

articles.title: NBA: Cameron Boozer tallies first triple-double, Grizzlies remain unbeaten
articles.summary: Pelicans earn first victory over still-winless Kings as Hawks withstand late push to hold off Cavaliers.
articles.body:
Rookie Cameron Boozer recorded 18 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists for his first career triple-double, and reserve Isaiah Stewart also scored 18 as the Memphis Grizzlies remained unbeaten with a solid 124-103 road victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.

Cedric Coward registered 17 points, seven rebounds and three steals, and Zach Edey added 13 points as Memphis improved to 5-0.

Backup GG Jackson scored 12 points while Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells and reserve Quinten Post added 10 points apiece for the Grizzlies, who outscored Portland 66-45 in the second half.

Deni Avdija had 24 points, nine rebounds and seven assists to pace the Trail Blazers.

Portland’s Ja Morant had 14 points and three assists in 23 minutes before departing in the fourth quarter due to a left hamstring injury.

Toumani Camara had 13 points and Donovan Clingan added 11 for the Trail Blazers. Damian Lillard had just nine points on 3-of-13 shooting.

A 3-pointer by Jerome gave Memphis a 101-89 advantage with 8:43 left in the contest and started a 13-0 burst. Coward drained a 3-pointer to conclude it and make it 111-89 with 5:31 remaining.

Wells scored on a layup to make it 117-93 with 3:52 left as Memphis cruised to the finish.

The game was tied at halftime but Memphis went on a 12-2 burst in the third quarter with Wells capping it with a 3-pointer to give the Grizzlies a 72-66 lead with 6:13 to play.

Portland later moved within two before Memphis rattled off 10 straight points. Coward culminated the run with a hoop to make it 87-75 with 2:09 remaining.

Lillard drove against former teammate Jerami Grant for a layup with 0.6 seconds left in the third as Portland trailed 91-83 entering the final stanza.

The contest was tied at 58 at halftime when Avdija scored 13 for Portland and Boozer had 13 for Memphis.

Pelicans earn first victory over still-winless Kings

Jeremiah Fears flirted with his first career triple-double and the New Orleans Pelicans broke into the win column for the first time this season with a 132-120 triumph over the visiting Sacramento Kings.

Fears and Zion Williamson each scored 22 points for New Orleans. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr poured in a season-best 34 points for Sacramento.

Derik Queen bookended a 12-0 burst early in the second quarter with a 3-pointer and a short jumper, allowing New Orleans to take a 36-32 advantage.

The Kings hung within 67-65 after an Acuff drive to the hoop in the second minute of the third period. But New Orleans then took command for good with a 21-4 flurry, in which Fears and Trey Murphy III drilled consecutive 3-pointers and Williamson contributed six points.

Sacramento still had a chance at 113-106 after a Zach LaVine 3-pointer with 7:11 to play, but New Orleans then ran off the next 10 points before coasting home.

Fears finished with his fourth career double-double, complementing his season-best point total with a career-best 13 assists.

Murphy chipped in with 19 points, Herbert Jones 16, Karlo Matkovic 12, and Saddiq Bey and Ben Mathurin 10 apiece for the Pelicans, who were playing for the second time on a three-game homestand. Williamson had five steals.

De’Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa had 24 points apiece, and LaVine totalled 21 for the Kings.

Hawks withstand late push to hold off Cavaliers

Onyeka Okongwu scored a season-high 29 points, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker sank two crucial free throws with 15.3 seconds remaining as the host Atlanta Hawks snapped a three-game losing streak with a 114-111 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Hawks led by 10 with 4:34 remaining, but Cleveland twice pulled within one point, the second time on Donovan Mitchell’s basket with 21 seconds left.

Okongwu went 11-for-17 from the field, including four 3-pointers, and added a season-high 12 rebounds. Alexander-Walker shot 8-for-17 from the field and also made four 3-pointers.

Aaron Wiggins added a season-high 20 points and seven rebounds off the bench, while Jalen Johnson scored 17.

Cleveland got a season-high 24 points from James Harden and 22 points from Mitchell. Sam Merrill came off the bench to make four 3-pointers and score 16.

Cleveland limited the Hawks to 23.8 percent shooting in the first quarter and, prompted by an early 10-3 run, took a 28-16 lead.

The Cavs led 35-24 with 7:22 left in the first half, but Atlanta went on a 13-2 run to tie at 4:33 on a runner by Okongwu. The Hawks took a 46-44 halftime lead.

Atlanta pushed its lead to 61-50 on Alexander-Walker’s 3-pointer with 9:14 left in the third quarter. Cleveland cut the margin to 83-82, fuelled by nine third-quarter points from Harden. Atlanta scored 43 points in the period and entered the fourth quarter with an 89-82 lead.

articles.title: La DGT hace un llamamiento para que recordemos esta norma que casi ningún conductor respeta
articles.standfirst: Es obligatoria desde este mismo año y los conductores debemos respetarla en situaciones de atasco o tráfico muy, muy lento
articles.summary: Es obligatoria desde este mismo año y los conductores debemos respetarla en situaciones de atasco o tráfico muy, muy lento
articles.body: Este viernes 30 de octubre se inicia la operación salida de un Puente de Todos los Santos que prevé 5,34 millones de desplazamientos por carretera. El foco está puesto en todas las carreteras principales de nuestro sistema radial, pero en esta ocasión resulta más imprevisible el volumen de tráfico que pueda acoger la autovía A-4, una vez que se encuentra suspendido el transporte de tren de alta velocidad que comunica Madrid con el sur de la península tras el trágico accidente de Urda. Este incremento de la circulación empezará a ser más intenso en la tarde de hoy viernes y la mañana del sábado. El domingo por la mañana los trayectos serán en general más cortos (los necesarios para acudir a la tradicional visita a los cementerios), con una vuelta a los viajes por carretera por la tarde para regresar a aquellas Comunidades Autónomas donde el lunes es día laborable. En las que, por el contrario, sea festivo, los atascos de entrada se prevén ya el lunes por la tarde. Aprovechando la inminente operación salida del Puente de Todos los Santos, la DGT ha aprovechado para recordarnos una norma que ya es obligatoria desde el 1 de octubre, pero que los conductores españoles todavía no estamos acostumbrados a respetar. Se trata de dejar el llamado Carril de Emergencia, aprobado en la última reforma del Reglamento General de Circulación mediante el Real Decreto 518/2026. En situaciones de atasco o circulación muy lenta (a paso de peatón), es habitual que los usuarios de una autovía ocupen los dos carriles y solo dejen un poco más de espacio en el arcén cuando oyen la sirena de un vehículo de emergencia que viene por detrás. Lo que la norma exige ahora es que, en autovías o autopistas con dos carriles por sentido con el mencionado atasco o la circulación muy lenta, los conductores del carril izquierdo se orillen hacia la izquierda y los del lado derecho se echen hacia el arcén. Esto debe ser así incluso cuando no esté viniendo un vehículo de emergencia. De esta forma, una ambulancia, coche de policía, Guardia Civil, camión de bomberos o grúa que deba acudir rápidamente a un siniestro podrá circular a más velocidad utilizando un espacio ya libre entre las dos filas de coches. Cuando por el contrario la vía sea de tres carriles, el carril de emergencia debe formarse entre el carril ubicado más a la izquierda y el central. Para ello, los del lado izquierdo deberán orillarse hacia la izquierda y los otros dos a la derecha. Esta norma no es nueva en el transporte por carretera ni la hemos inventado en España. En Alemania la ponen en práctica los conductores desde hace más de cuatro décadas, por lo que allí lo sorprendente es que algún conductor no la respete. E incluso en países como Francia o Austria ya se está convirtiendo en costumbre. Conviene tener en cuenta que no facilitar la formación de este nuevo carril de emergencia se considera una infracción grave y acarrea una multa de 200 euros.

articles.title: Sharp-shooting Dream beat Valkyries 80-69 to force Game 7 in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream made sure the series went the distance with an 80-69 victory over the visiting Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
The WNBA had numerous reasons to expand the Finals from five games ahead of the 2025 season.

Now in Year 2 of the revamped format, the league will hold its first-ever Game 7 with a first-time champion awaiting on either side.

The fourth-seeded Atlanta Dream made sure the series went the distance, leaving no doubt in an 80-69 victory over the visiting second-seeded Golden State Valkyries on Thursday afternoon.

“It’s such a great opportunity. I think our team is ready for it,” Atlanta head coach Karl Smesko said of the winner-take-all game on Saturday night in San Francisco.

“We’ll take the next day to get as prepared as we can and make any adjustments that need to be made. … There’s a mentality right now of, ‘We’re happy we won, but we know the job is not done.’ We’ve got one more game. We expect to go out there and play great.”

Allisha Gray, hampered by a hand injury throughout the postseason, scored 23 points on five 3-pointers in a Game 6 that saw the Dream connect on 13 3-pointers while holding Golden State to 26 first-half points.

Rhyne Howard added 21 points and Angel Reese posted 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists for Atlanta, which didn’t trail after the game’s opening minute. Jordin Canada chipped in 10 points in a win under unusual circumstances.

The game was turned into a matinee by the league, which pushed the start time up to accommodate the Atlanta Hawks’ home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night.

Despite the awkward tip time, a packed State Farm Arena saw the biggest win in franchise history — so far.

“First, shoutout to the crowd,” Reese said. “To be able to come here at 12:30 on a Thursday with so many things going on in the world from school to work, we’re just super thankful. We fed off their energy. They were super loud from the beginning.”

Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points, while Tiffany Hayes scored 15. Golden State, still in just its second season in the league, made just seven of its 27 3-point attempts (25.9 percent).

“I want to go back and look at the film and find solutions on where my message wasn’t delivered correctly,” Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase said. “I’ll give them some space right now to rest and recover, but then probably have some reflection moments on the plane ride home.”

After Williams made a free throw to cut Golden State’s early deficit to 6-5, Atlanta rattled off 13 straight points — including five apiece from Gray and Canada — to give the Dream a 19-5 edge.

Williams stopped the bleeding with the Valkyries’ first 3-pointer of the game, but that was answered with consecutive Howard treys to make it 25-8.

Atlanta made six of eight 3-pointers in the first quarter and took a 32-15 lead into the second.

“It was just frustrating,” Nakase said of the Valkyries’ first quarter. “The poor start was unacceptable.”

The Dream’s offensive barrage continued into the second quarter, as Reese’s first 3-pointer and a mid-range jumper by Howard extended the margin to 25 with 4:20 left in the first half.

Hayes made a triple and reserve Laeticia Amihere closed the first half with a layup to cut Golden State’s halftime deficit to 46-26.

The Valkyries outscored Atlanta 21-17 in the third quarter and pulled within 16 on Kaila Charles’ buzzer-beating 3-pointer.

Golden State continued to trim Atlanta’s lead in the fourth, as Williams’ layup made it 68-55 with 6:50 remaining.

The Dream then responded with 3-pointers by Gray and Reese to push the lead back to 19.

Williams completed a three-point play at the 1:15 mark to pull the Valkyries within eight, but Gray sank her fifth trey on the other end to stamp Atlanta’s pivotal victory.

Gray, a 10-year veteran, will be one of the many members of the Dream in search of their first championship at the Chase Center on Saturday.

“We know when we play Atlanta Dream basketball and support each other and move the ball, we’re successful,” Gray said. “The biggest thing for us is just executing our offence.”

articles.title: Javi Leal sustituye a Ale Galán en la convocatoria de España para el Mundial de pádel
articles.standfirst: El gaditano de 23 años suple al madrileño en la lista de ocho integrantes
articles.summary: El gaditano de 23 años suple al madrileño en la lista de ocho integrantes
articles.body: Durante la mañana de este viernes se ha hecho oficial que Alejandro Galán no podrá acudir al Mundial de pádel con España la próxima semana en Doha (Qatar). Una baja muy sensible para Juanjo Gutiérrez, que ya ha anunciado al que será su sustituto en la lista: Javi Leal. El jugador de El Puerto de Santa María, de 23 años, estuvo a punto de entrar en la formación española para la cita mundialista, pero el seleccionador se acabó decantando por el navarro Aimar Goñi como cuarto revés tras Galán, Navarro y Nieto. Finalmente, tendrá su oportunidad tras lo sucedido con Ale. Leal ya sabe lo que es vestir la camiseta de La Roja, con la que ganó el Europeo absoluto del año 2024, pero será su debut en una cita de este calibre, al igual que Goñi. En su palmarés también cuenta con dos campeonatos del mundo de menores logrados en 2017 y 2019, cuando apenas tenía 14 y 16 años. Por tanto, la formación definitiva de España, que buscará su quinto mundial y romper una racha de dos títulos consecutivos de Argentina, queda de la siguiente manera: Coki Nieto, Paquito Navarro, Aimar Goñi y Javi Leal como jugadores de revés, y con Arturo Coello, Juan Lebrón, Mike Yanguas y Jon Sanz como jugadores de derecha. Un jugador que este año está mostrando su mejor versión al lado de Fran Guerrero, con el que inició su tercera etapa en el mes de mayo tras haber empezado la temporada al lado de Pablo Cardona, quien tuvo que parar de nuevo debido a sus lesiones de rodilla y cuya dolencia provocó que Leal tuviese que saltar de compañero en compañero de forma profesional… hasta volver con Fran. En este 2026, Leal ha ganado tres títulos del Cupra FIP Tour, los Platinum de Marsella, Oeiras y Lyon, y ha alcanzado su primera final de Premier Padel al lado de Guerrero. Fue en Pretoria (Sudáfrica), donde acabaron cayendo a manos de Alejandro Galán y Fede Chingotto. A estos números también se añaden unas semifinales (Valladolid) y cuatro cuartos de final que le hace estar más cerca de disputar el Tour Finals de Barcelona.

articles.title: 'Karateka' o cómo sonreír a la vida a pesar de las heridas
articles.standfirst: Sandra Sánchez, Jesús del Moral y los actores Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado, que les dan vida en la película, relatan los secretos del rodaje de la película en MARCA
articles.summary: Sandra Sánchez, Jesús del Moral y los actores Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado, que les dan vida en la película, relatan los secretos del rodaje de la película en MARCA
articles.body: Sandra Sánchez ejerce de anfitriona. En MARCA se siente como en casa. Con su habitual sonrisa muestra orgullosa su foto en la Galería de los MARCA Leyenda. Jesús del Moral, sin quien no se entendería la carrera de la mejor karateka de todos los tiempos, conoce tan bien como ella esta redacción. En cambio, la otra ‘Sandra’ y el otro ‘Jesús’ viven esta experiencia por primera vez. Son Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado, su dos clones cinematográficos en la película ‘Karateka’ que se estrena hoy. Ambos miran esa sucesión de estrellas del deporte que se asemeja al Paseo de la Fama de Hollywood. “Si está Jordan...”, comenta Criado. Hace cinco años el director Aritz Moreno conoció la historia de Sandra Sánchez. “Esto es una peli”, dijo de inmediato. El guion, plasmado en imágenes, recorre la trayectoria de la campeona olímpica: sus orígenes en Talavera de la Reina, el paso por el CAR de Madrid, la renuncia al equipo nacional por la enfermedad de su madre y el complicado camino de regreso a la élite cuando nadie creía en ella. Allí se unió a Jesús del Moral, entrenador, primero; pareja, después. Los dos caminaron juntos hasta el oro olímpico. “Todavía me tengo que pellizcar para saber que esto es real. Debo gestionar muchas emociones porque se reabren muchas heridas al reencontrarme con esa Sandrita ingenua adolescente con ganas de ver todo bonito en la vida y que tuvo que pasar por todo lo que pasó”, comenta Sánchez. Andrea Ros descubrió a la karateka cuando Aritz Moreno le enseñó un vídeo de la final olímpica de Tokio. El director le avanzó que quería hacer una película sobre ella. “Y yo también, le dije. Sin saber todavía si pasaría el casting ya me puse a ver los vídeos habidos y por haber de Sandra desde 2013”, recuerda la actriz. Andrea es Sandra: “El fuego que tiene dentro yo también lo tengo”. Y Sandra es Andrea. “Hay mucho de mí y mucho de ella también. Ella comparte conmigo muchas experiencias que son duras y cómo cada una las hemos enfrentado. Andrea las ha tenido que hacer muy suyas para luego poder transmitirlas. Me gusta una escena cuando ella, después de varias cosas malas que pasan, sale y me veo a mí misma sonriéndole a la vida a pesar de haber vivido lo que he vivido”, rememora Sandra. Andrea asiente: “Puse mis heridas al servicio de Sandra”. Cuando Andrea llevaba seis meses de preparación, llegó Patrick Criado. “Vi el nivel que había alcanzado y a dónde había que llegar. Jesús es muy exigente desde un punto positivo. Es una exigencia de llegar a ser un poquito mejor cada día en lo que tú puedas hacer y en lo que está en tu mano. Me he llevado ese aprendizaje”, recuerda Criado. Jesús del Moral echa la vista atrás hasta hace tres años para ponderar la evolución de Andrea Ros. “El primer día era incapaz de hacer una flexión bien hecha. Y mira lo que ha hecho esta mujer. Al principio pasó por el proceso de frustrarse porque quería llegar a ser como Sandra, pero eso era imposible. Luego se dio cuenta de que debía llegar hasta el nivel que pudiera. De lo que se trataba era de mostrar la esencia de Sandra. Cuando lo entendió, empezó a disfrutar, a transmitir”, explica Del Moral. “En ese primer entreno yo tenía la sensación de que me iba a morir. Pensaba ‘bueno, sabe lo que hace, es su trabajo, si ve que me muero, hará algo para pararlo”, apostilla Ros entre risas, antes de elogiar el método de Jesús: “Tiene una forma de enseñar muy especial. No te das cuenta nunca de cuando lo haces bien. Te va subiendo el listón porque el objetivo es ir lo más lejos posible”. Criado entra al quite: “Me ha venido un flash de Jesús cuando entrenabas y hacías un movimiento que tú pensabas que estaba bien y él te lo hacía hacer otra vez. Y tú lo haces con una sonrisa”. La charla entre los cuatro protagonistas de ‘Karateka’ prosigue en un ambiente distendido. “Aritz y Jesús tiene algo en común. Si les decepcionas no te lo muestran. Y eso a mí me da alas. Es lo que hace Aritz conmigo como actriz. Yo puedo porque él cree que puedo”, comenta Ros. La simbiosis entre director y entrenador fue perfecta. Aritz sabía qué necesitaba de cada intérprete, lo que permitió a Jesús planificar el entrenamiento de karate necesario para cada uno. Andrea y Patrick sacan a relucir la exigencia de Del Moral: “Si era un plano medio y pensabas que no tenías que hacer nada con las piernas, Jesús te decía que sí, porque se nota en el resto del cuerpo”. “Queríamos que cualquier persona de karate que vea la película, viese su karate y pueda decir lo bien que lo hacen”, apunta Del Moral. Las similitudes entre la carrera artística y deportiva centra ahora la conversación. “En ambas hay una incertidumbre y una dependencia a veces de lo ajeno que no puedes controlar”, apunta Criado. “Son mundos muy injustos con quien llega porque depende de muchos factores y en ambos de muchas cosas que pasan por despachos que dirigen hombres mayores y eso tiene un impacto en nuestras vidas muy grande”, recalca Ros. La película, producida por Atresmedia Cine y Sr. y Sra., y distribuida por Warner Bros. Pictures Spain, ha dejado huella en los dos protagonistas. “He aprendido que Sandra y Jesús viven en el presente e intentan mejorar cada día en lo que son, en lo que hacen y no miran atrás con resentimiento. Se ve el amor entre ellos y el que tienen por su profesión. Es un aprendizaje que yo me llevo en la vida para siempre y por el que siempre les estaré eternamente agradecido”, sentencia Criado. Andrea incide: “Me han traído mucho temple a mi vida. Me han dado raíz porque siempre he sido como muy volátil, casi como ansiosa por las cosas. Y luego está lo que ha significado paralelamente esta película para mi carrera. Me voy a acordar toda mi vida de que si hoy estoy así de serena es porque les he conocido a ellos”. A Criado la película le ha avivado su visión del deportista. “Necesita una disciplina para llegar a ser el mejor que pueda ser, independientemente del rival. Eso lo traslado a mi profesión. Los entrenamientos del deporte de élite los puedo extrapolar a a mi trabajo. Y si se me olvida, llamo a Jesús y aparece con el palo”, comenta riendo. Así llegaron y así se marcharon. ‘Smile and relax’.

articles.title: AFCON returns to 2-year cycle after CAF reverses quadrennial decision
articles.summary: Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will cohost the next AFCON in 2027, with subsequent tournaments in 2028, 2031 and 2033.
articles.body:
The Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) will be held every two years, not four as was planned, governing body the Confederation of African Football (CAF) announced after reversing an earlier decision.

AFCON has traditionally been staged every two years, but CAF’s surprise decision last December to move to a four-year cycle was not widely welcomed.

“The Confederation of African Football (CAF) Executive Committee today unanimously decided that the CAF Africa Cup of Nations will return to taking place every Two Years,” CAF said in a statement.

Under the previous plan, AFCON would have moved to a four-year cycle, with the proposed CAF Nations League becoming the continent’s biennial competition.

CAF President Patrice Motsepe said at a strategy conference in Cape Verde earlier this month that the organisation was considering returning AFCON to a two-year cycle.

CAF said the Nations League would take years to generate enough revenue to sustain African football.

“The decision by the CAF Executive Committee to reinstate the organization of the AFCON every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 CAF Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent,” Motsepe said in a statement.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will cohost the next edition in 2027, with subsequent tournaments to be held in 2028, 2031 and 2033.

There will be no AFCON in 2030, with CAF maintaining its tradition of not staging the tournament in a World Cup year.

articles.title: Dakar Rally 2027 to be held in Portugal, Morocco as Saudi hosting revoked
articles.summary: Organisers say moving Dakar Rally, likely scheduled January 9-23, out of Saudi Arabia was ‘exceptional and one-off’.
articles.body:
The 2027 edition of the Dakar Rally will be held in Morocco following a prologue and first stage in Portugal, organisers Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) said, five days after announcing the event would not be held in Saudi Arabia due to security concerns.

“The Algarve will host the prologue and the first special stage. Morocco, with the aim of exploring its territory in its entirety, from north to far south, will host 11 stages and a rest day in Agadir,” ASO said in a statement.

The 49th edition of the Dakar Rally, initially scheduled to run from January 1 to January 15, will now take place from January 9 to January 23, subject to approval by the International Automobile Federation (FIA)’s World Motor Sport Council.

“The relocated 49th edition of the Dakar will meet the sporting standards that have always made it the most demanding rally-raid event,” Dakar director David Castera said.

“Despite the short timeframe we have had to work with, we have designed a true Dakar.”

Dakar 2027 will feature a total distance of 7,824km (4,862 miles), including 4,341km (2,697 miles) of special stages, from Loule-Faro to Marrakesh.

ASO said on Sunday that the decision to move the race out of Saudi Arabia was “exceptional and one-off”. The 50th edition of the Dakar Rally in 2028 would return to the kingdom, which has hosted the event since 2020.

Morocco hosting the race means the Dakar Rally will return to Africa for the first time since 2008.

The event started in 1978 as a race from Paris across the Sahara to the Senegalese capital Dakar in West Africa, and has long been regarded as the world’s toughest motorsport challenge.

It was later staged in South America between 2009 and 2019 after leaving Africa for security reasons.

articles.title: Hennessy, horses and huge money: Inside the most important horse auction in the world
articles.summary: The Keeneland September Yearling Sale is the world’s most important horse auction. Take a look inside the expensive heart of horse racing.
articles.body: Perched on a stool at a high-top table, his back against a window at the farthest recess of a very crowded room, Bill Farish wears a white ballcap, a vest over a blue-checked shirt and a pair of khakis. He rests his chin on his left hand and, every now and again, he casually raises his index finger. To his right sits Cherie DeVaux, trainer of Golden Tempo, the 2026 Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner. To his left sits Terry Finley, president of West Point Thoroughbreds and part owner of Always Dreaming, the 2017 Derby winner. At the table directly in front of them, Marshawn Lynch – wearing a pair of three-quarter-length sweats and a T-shirt – sips on some Hennessy. They are all staring at a striking dark bay colt foaled on May 6 of last year. Hip 39, as the horse is known, has just been walked up a chute and onto a stage, and the cacophony created by a roomful of people clearly has him agitated. Just a few days ago, the son of 2016 Derby winner Nyquist roamed freely around the fields of nearby Gainesway Farm, a 1,500-acre pastoral equine playground whose history predates US independence. Now, Hip 39 is one of 4,642 horses up for sale at the annual September Yearling Sale at Keeneland racetrack. The sale is everything the Derby is not. All business, no pretense. These are true horse people, and whether blessed with generational wealth or fresh money, they are here to do work, not to be seen. People distractedly pluck hors d’oeuvres or cocktails from servers walking around with trays, more interested in the breeding information on their iPads than the catering. There are no Instagrammable photo ops or fancy hats, just people in jeans, T-shirts, cowboy boots and shorts. Former Philadelphia Phillies slugger Jayson Werth, in a wrinkled T-shirt and camouflage shorts, is nearly unrecognizable, his famous cascade of hair tucked under a ballcap. And when DeVaux sits alongside Lynch to talk horses, a woman nervously approaches their table to ask for a picture – of the horse trainer, not the former Super Bowl-winning, five-time Pro Bowl running back. But this is where the first Saturday in May gets its start. It takes money to nourish a Derby dream at the Keeneland sales, but here, the real currency is hope. “Any one of them,” DeVaux says, “could be the one.” Today, she hopes her next Derby winner might be Hip 39. Which is why Farish, the general manager of Lane’s End Farm and part of a four-group partnership that includes DeVaux’s Belladonna Racing, keeps raising his finger. Each seemingly meaningless twitch signals a bid worth between $50,000 and $100,000, depending on the auctioneer’s ask. After less than two minutes of bidding, Farish has twitched his way to securing Hip 39 for $1.2 million. Later in the day, the partnership will nab two more colts for $375,000 and $800,000 respectively, and by the end of the two-week sale, will have purchased 20 horses for a cool $15.48 million. And not a single one of them has ever so much as felt a saddle on his back. ‘Only $400,000?’ Lexington is the sort of place where the arrival of your luggage at a baggage claim carousel is accompanied by the bugle strains of the call to the post, where Citation Boulevard hugs the north edges of the city and Man o’War Boulevard the south. Louisville, a 75-mile ride west, might be the country’s epicenter of racing, but Lexington is about the horses. The university’s Big Blue Nation is outnumbered only by the big bluebloods. Generational wealth with an eye for thoroughbreds took root here long ago, drawn by the limestone-rich soil and lush bluegrass that is especially good for foals. Most of the people who own the farms got rich elsewhere first – the Farish family’s roots go back to the Texas oil rush – and then got richer breeding, selling and racing horses. Theirs is the sort of money that comes without ostentation, where people don’t flaunt their wealth but it’s clear they have it. “We’re getting ready to leave a little early,” a man says into his phone while heading to the valet parking area near the sale. “Can you call the pilot and let them know we’re ready to go?” Minutes later, another man – wearing a fedora and martini-glass shirt while toting his wheezing bulldog on a pink leash – follows and heads to his high-end SUV. “It’s crazy,” says Werth, no pauper himself. “A horse sells for $400,000 and you’re thinking, ‘Only $400,000? What’s wrong with it?’ Someone just spent $400,000 on a freaking horse.” Kentuckians had been racing for decades before Keeneland opened its doors, cutting dirt ovals in the early 1800s after the city banned racing in the street. Keeneland hosted its first race in 1936, but the track’s trajectory changed during World War II, when railroad restrictions prevented local breeders from shipping their horses north to the sale in Saratoga, New York. To accommodate local horse owners, Keeneland erected a tent for a makeshift auction. The first sale, in 1943, went so well – 312 horses sold for an average of $2,979 – that the next year, after Lexington-based Fasig-Tipton decided to shutter its own sales paddock, the local group bought, deconstructed and rebuilt its sales arena. It’s the same one used today. At the first September yearling sale inside the pavilion, 92 horses were purchased for a grand total of $419,100. During this year’s two-week sale, buyers purchased 2,856 horses for a world-record $536,737,900. Seventy yearlings sold for more than $1 million, another world record, and one, a colt from leading sire Into Mischief, went for $3.7 million. Though Keeneland still has big races with attractive purses – its annual Blue Grass Stakes is a key qualifier for Derby contenders and this weekend, it will host the Breeders’ Cup for the fourth time – it has just 32 days of live racing in the spring and fall. The real business is in the sales. “Lots of people in Lexington, they love racing, but they walk by these doors, and they have no idea what goes on in here,” says Tony Lacy, Keeneland vice president of sales. “This is horse racing’s NBA or NFL Draft.” DeVaux’s big moment At 11 a.m. on Monday, just two hours before the sale officially begins, DeVaux is out in front of Barn 29. She “slept in” today, which means she woke up at 5:30 in the morning. Yearlings arrive at Keeneland based on where they are placed in what’s known as the books. Created by the Keeneland sales team, the books set the schedule for the two-week sale and sort the horses into a sort of pedigree ranking. The perceived best horses, and likely the most expensive, are for sale in Book 1 on Monday and Tuesday. Book 2 is Wednesday, all the way down to Book 12. In an event where everything comes with a price tag, even the simple slotting of horses can prove perilous. Lacy has heard plenty of kvetching from breeders who believe their horses to be undervalued in the book, and thereby potentially undervalued in the sale. “My hair was not this gray a week ago,” he says with a shake of his head. Because it is now Monday, DeVaux is evaluating horses in Book 4. (Book 1 horses arrived on Friday). Her husband, bloodstock agent David Ingordo, has created what’s called a short list, spending months “here, there and everywhere,” as DeVaux puts it, on farms eyeing up many of the horses since they were foals. From his searches, he whittles down the available horses to the ones the team is interested in purchasing. On Monday, the team is considering 12 of the 185 horses available. Since winning the Derby and Belmont, DeVaux’s opportunities have grown monumentally. She has tried to stay true to herself, relying as always on her husband’s knowledge and her own instincts, and not get wide-eyed as opportunities that once eluded her now practically fall at her feet. “Now that we’ve done it once, people want us to prove that we can do it again,” she says. It helps that DeVaux is decisive. She is as self-assured about what she likes in a horse as she is about what she wants in the remodel of her New Orleans home. “Contractors hate me,” she says with a laugh. Horse folks not so much. DeVaux is greeted warmly by the various sellers and breeders as she views their horses and wastes no one’s time. Where some trainers might ask a groom to walk a horse multiple times, DeVaux is usually good with an up and back. She eyes whether their feet flop or land nicely and looks for broad backsides that house the literal horsepower to race. She considers age, whether the horse was a late or early foal, when sizing up its maturity and body development, and values temperament as much as conformation. A year ago, she knocked a horse off the team’s short list, unhappy that it grew too agitated during the morning viewing. She also looks for something that can’t be measured, a glimmer in the eye or a spark of personality. She ends each check by petting the horse and giving it a little talking-to. “I like that one,” she says of one as he walks away. “He’s plucky.” Every horse is vetted for soundness, the buyers given detailed reports about its health, but DeVaux trusts herself as much as anyone. Despite eyeing hundreds of horses, she can recall each one by memory, barely needing to refer to her notes. Grabbing a quick bite to eat before the sale, she pulls up photos of the yearlings she’s considered as if they’re baby pictures, cooing over their “big fat faces.” There is, of course, no guarantee of anything. DeVaux’s ride to glory came via Golden Tempo, a homebred, which means he was born and raised by his owner and never sold at auction. “Nobody would have bought him at the sale,” DeVaux says. “If you looked at him, no one would have been interested.” In six starts, he has three wins, including two legs of the Triple Crown, and has earned $4.75 million. On the other end of the return-on-investment spectrum is Green Monkey. Sold as a two-year-old in 2006 for a record $16 million, the horse raced three times, never finishing better than third. “What’s that saying about a piece of art?” asks Curt Ramsey, Lane’s End director of equine operations, as he watches DeVaux evaluate his horses. “It’s worth what someone is willing to pay for it.” An expensive dance Ryan Mahan sits in a courtyard outside the pavilion, enjoying a break after running his mouth for an hour straight. Next November will be his 50th working at Keeneland. He’s held a number of jobs during those five decades, but for the last 25 has provided the literal hum to the sales as the lead auctioneer. Mahan’s love of horses comes naturally. His stepfather, Robert Copelan, who recently turned 100 years young, worked as a racetrack vet and Mahan tagged along while he made his rounds. In 1973, Mahan held the halter of a Derby entrant while Copelan treated a troublesome abscess with hot compresses. The horse healed. His name was Secretariat. Mahan thought he wanted to follow in Copelan’s footsteps, but when he came to his first sale, he grew wide-eyed at what he calls the “belly-to-belly commerce” side of horse racing. He went to auctioneer school. “It’s kind of like karaoke,” he says. “You know you’re going to feel stupid when it’s your turn, but if there are 200 people in class, they all feel stupid, too,” and started his career selling goats and chickens at small farm auctions before graduating to thoroughbreds. In 2001, when lead auctioneer Tom Caldwell passed away, Mahan took over at Keeneland. It is a unique job, requiring both unflappable steadiness and the flair of a showman. Mahan knows many of the breeders and buyers personally and isn’t afraid to needle them to keep the bidding going. “Don’t stop now,” he says mid-auction of a horse that has reached $950,000. “I don’t care if it’s $2,000 or $2 million, you have a minute to decide because the guy next to you is going to bid, and then it’s over,” Mahan says. “It’s very high risk so the least I can do is make it fun.” Mahan’s longevity is true to Keeneland’s commitment to tradition. While it’s adjusted to suit the times – bids can be made both by phone and online – it prefers to keep things both highbrow and unchanged. In 2026, the man known as Beast Mode sipped his Hennessy from a similar perch that housed Queen Elizabeth in 1984. Those who work the sales are as much a part of the fabric as the place itself. A few years ago, someone asked Mahan how he might get into the business. “Well,” Mahan told him, “the newest guy we hired, we call him Pup. He’s 60.” The consistency is as practical as it is parochial. To watch a horse sale is to witness a well-choreographed dance, or an orchestra in perfect concert. Mahan and the public address announcer sit at a raised rostrum directly behind the sale ring and in front of the pavilion full of people. The horses exit one of the 55 barns on the back of the property and are led to a paddock area to parade in front of interested buyers. When it’s their turn, the yearlings are led into the sales ring by a groom and handed over to a showman, a veritable horse whisperer who can calm stressed-out yearlings as they whinny, pace and sometimes downright refuse to walk into the ring (in that case, they’re often backed in, so they don’t know what’s coming). The spotters stand at the end of each of the aisles of the theatre-like seating area, with their backs to the horses and their eyes scanning the crowd for the slightest tick of movement to signal a bid. Everyone has their tell. Farish flicks his finger. Others tip a cap or slide a pin. Back in his day, legendary trainer D. Wayne Lukas would use a pen in his pocket to signal his interest – once he removed it, he was out of the bidding – while famed trainer Bob Baffert simply waves. When a spotter eyes a bid, he gives a loud call to Mahan who drumbeats the auction forward. Another spotter sits behind Mahan in a raised plexiglass booth, looking out at the paddock area that the horses have just exited. Buyers are equal parts superstitious and surreptitious. Some sit in the same spot to make their bids; others only work with certain spotters – Mahan once pulled spotter Bo Black away from his lunch mid-bite because a purchaser would only bid if Black was in front of him. And more than a few prefer to keep their action private, never entering the ring at all lest anyone else gloms onto their interest. They make their bids from the paddocks to the man in the box. All the while, someone mans a phone for internet bids, all of it funneled to Mahan, who keeps the auction going. It feels and looks like organized chaos, a rinse-and-repeat of white noise that churns on for hours with no break. No sooner does Hip 1 walk out after being sold (for $700,000) than the public address announcer runs through the bona fides of Hip 2 as the horse enters the ring. Once a horse is sold, another green-blazered courier heads to the purchaser, handing over a paper receipt that looks like it’s straight out of a 1980s Radio Shack, complete with a white, yellow and pink copy. After the gavel drops on Hip 39, a courier arrives almost immediately at Farish, Finley and DeVaux’s table. Finley signs the receipt, takes his yellow copy and folds it, before casually shoving it in his back pocket, as if he just bought a stereo with an eight-track player, and not a million-dollar horse. “It’s the game,” he says. “Out of all of these horses, maybe we know the names of five or six of them. Maybe.” Why the ridiculous prices are worth it Bob Baffert grabs a water out of a nearby cooler to keep the searing heat and humidity at bay. No North American trainer has acquired more expensive horseflesh in the 21st century than Baffert, including a $10 million 2-year-old that came into his barn earlier this year. But Baffert’s introduction to the Keeneland Sales was far different. He motions toward a cement wall outside a nearby barn. “That’s where we watched the horses the first time I came here,” says the two-time Triple Crown winner. It was 1988 and Baffert, who was just starting to pivot away from training quarter horses to thoroughbreds, only got to Lexington after worming his way onto the private plane of wealthy track owner, R.D. Hubbard. From his perch on the wall, Baffert keyed in on Hip 1752, a big gray, but with no real buying partners, convinced a fellow quarter horse trainer to go in with him. The man agreed but said he would go no higher than $20,000. When the bidding escalated beyond his threshold, Baffert’s money man backed out, but the trainer, too far gone on the horse, kept raising his hand. When the gavel dropped, he had agreed to pay $30,000. “I was thinking, please someone offer $30,001,” Baffert says. “But no one did.” After signing for the sale, Baffert was almost immediately summoned to the sales office. He had no credit on file and had to prove he could pay for the horse. He pulled a check out of his wallet, and only after the sales team called his bank to verify he was good for the money did Baffert get the horse. Hip 1752 became Thirty Slews. He won the Breeders’ Cup Sprint, Baffert’s first Grade 1 race win (he now has 266), and earned $825,000 across his career. “When I first came here, I thought, ‘This is ridiculous.’ You could buy a house for the prices and make payments for 30 years,” Baffert says. “But when you win the Kentucky Derby, you say, ‘Oh, I get it.’ You can’t put a price on that feeling, or the price on the feeling you get when any horse wins a race. That’s what makes this all worth it.” It is the entirety of it, really. Werth, the ex-Phillies and Nationals slugger, came to Keeneland for the first time in 2022. With his baseball career over, he was looking for a similar adrenaline rush, and a friend turned him on to horse racing. He knew less than nothing about horses but went to the sale anyway. During the third session, he aimlessly crossed the paddock area and turned left, running into trainer Danny Gargan. The two chatted, and Werth explained that he was interested in buying a filly. Gargan talked him into keying in on a colt he liked, guessing rightly that Werth’s celebrity status would add some cachet to the purchase. Werth put up 10% of the $325,000 to purchase Hip 391, who would become Dornoch and led Werth to the 2024 Belmont Stakes winner’s circle. “If I turned right, who knows?” says Werth as he watches the horses for sale. “I might be playing golf in Ireland. This whole thing is absurd. It’s like buying a Little Leaguer and hoping he makes the World Series, but it is such a rush. That’s why we’re here.” Having a little self-control amid the madness After securing the first three horses they bid on, the Faris-Finley-DeVaux group’s luck stalled. They finished as underbidders (one notch below the purchasers) a few times and opted to back out on others. They set their max price on one yearling at $1.4 million; it went for $2.3, and they quit at $1.4 million on another that went for $100,000 more. “You have to have a little self-control,” DeVaux says. “It’s hard. I mean, I’m the queen of one more bid, but you can’t think that way. You really can’t.” As day one of the sale winds down, Ingordo decides to switch things up. He heads out to the paddock area, leaning up against a rail directly in front of the spotter perched at the window. He eyes up Hip 181, a dark brown colt, and does the bidding himself. Ingordo bids aggressively, but a Japanese gentleman next to him, his phone pressed to his ear the entire time, one-ups him. The horse sells for $2.1 million and, as the giddy winner grins and yells into his phone, Ingordo shrugs. “Thought we had him,” he says. The team shuffles to the exits. It’s 6:30 p.m., five-and-a-half hours after the sale started and nearly 12 hours since DeVaux got to the track. Back home, someone is preparing food for the team, but they will not eat leisurely. There are 15 more days of sales, with 4,458 more horses to consider. And one of them just might be the one.

articles.title: Matteo Moretto desvela el equipo que quiere fichar a Fermín López y Pablo Barrios
articles.standfirst: El periodista italiano explica en La Pizarra que un equipo de la Premier ha sondeado a los dos centrocampistas. También habla del interés del Barça en Nathan y Bastoni y del futuro de Jacobo Ramón.
articles.summary: El periodista italiano explica en La Pizarra que un equipo de la Premier ha sondeado a los dos centrocampistas. También habla del interés del Barça en Nathan y Bastoni y del futuro de Jacobo Ramón.
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes empieza a dejar movimientos de cara a las próximas ventanas y el Manchester United ya trabaja en la búsqueda de nuevos centrocampistas. Así lo ha desvelado Matteo Moretto en La Pizarra de Radio MARCA, donde ha señalado a dos nombres propios de LaLiga: Pablo Barrios y Fermín López. El periodista italiano ha explicado que el conjunto inglés ha preguntado por ambos futbolistas, aunque ha aclarado que, por el momento, no existe ninguna negociación abierta. "Hay un club en la Premier que es el Manchester United que tiene muchas cosas que arreglar y que está buscando un perfil de centrocampista que tenga las características de Barrios y Fermín. Ha preguntado por ambos, no hay negociación, simplemente hay un sondeo", ha explicado Moretto. El interés del conjunto inglés no se presenta como una operación sencilla. Tanto el Atlético de Madrid como el Barcelona consideran a sus respectivos centrocampistas piezas importantes de sus proyectos deportivos y no tienen intención de facilitar sus salidas. "Es muy complicado que ambos salgan. Pablo Barrios es un jugador imprescindible para el Atlético y Fermín es clave para el Barça, pero el United está buscando ese tipo de perfiles", ha señalado el periodista. Moretto también ha desvelado que el club inglés aprovechó su reciente visita a Madrid para disputar la Champions League para mantener diferentes encuentros. "Cuando vinieron a Madrid a jugar la Champions aprovecharon para tener muchas reuniones", ha añadido. En clave azulgrana, Moretto ha anticipado que el Barcelona podría escuchar ofertas por algunos de sus futbolistas importantes entre el mercado de enero y el próximo verano. Uno de los nombres que ha puesto sobre la mesa es el de Jules Koundé, cuyo futuro vuelve a estar en el aire. "Entre enero y verano seguro que el Barça escuchará ofertas por algunos de sus titulares. Koundé tiene papeletas para salir", ha desvelado el periodista italiano. Una situación que podría estar relacionada con los movimientos que prepara el conjunto azulgrana para reforzar su plantilla, especialmente en la línea defensiva. Otro de los nombres propios de la intervención ha sido Nathan, central del Betis, que aparece relacionado con el Barcelona. El conjunto azulgrana busca un defensa que encaje en las características que demanda Hansi Flick y el futbolista brasileño reúne algunas de las condiciones que busca el club. Además, el periodista ha desvelado un detalle importante sobre la situación del futbolista: Nathan ha iniciado los trámites para obtener el pasaporte español. Un movimiento que podría facilitar una hipotética operación, ya que dejaría de ocupar plaza de extracomunitario. Eso sí, su llegada no sería sencilla desde el punto de vista económico. "El Betis pediría mucho dinero", ha advertido Moretto. Otro de los centrales que ha estado relacionado con el Barcelona durante los últimos meses es Alessandro Bastoni. El defensa del Inter de Milán ha sido uno de los nombres que más han sonado en clave azulgrana, aunque su posible llegada no recibió el visto bueno definitivo de Hansi Flick. "Hemos hablado mucho de Bastoni en clave Barça en estos últimos meses. No se dio el fichaje porque Flick no dio luz verde a su fichaje", ha explicado Moretto. La situación podría cambiar de cara al próximo verano si aparece una oferta importante. El periodista ha señalado que tanto el futbolista como el Inter están contentos con su situación actual, pero ha dejado abierta la posibilidad de una salida si llega una propuesta económica difícil de rechazar. "Bastoni y el Inter están contentos, pero de cara a verano, si llega una oferta muy alta, el Inter podría escucharla para dejarle marchar", ha asegurado. Por último, Moretto también ha repasado la situación de Jacobo Ramón, que está destacando con el Como. El Real Madrid sigue muy pendiente de la evolución del central y estudia ejecutar la opción que tiene para recuperarlo por una cantidad inferior a los nueve millones de euros. La intención del conjunto blanco sería recuperar al defensa, aunque todavía está por decidir qué papel tendría en la primera plantilla. "El Madrid sabe que puede volver a ficharle por menos de nueve millones, que es un precio muy barato. La idea del Real Madrid es traerlo de vuelta, pero luego veremos qué pasa con el futbolista", ha explicado. Moretto también ha desvelado que Jacobo Ramón todavía no ha hablado con José Mourinho sobre su futuro y que esa conversación deberá producirse más adelante. "Jacobo no ha hablado con Mourinho aún, esto se solucionará entre marzo y abril", ha apuntado. La previsión del periodista es que el Real Madrid termine recuperando al futbolista, aunque su continuidad en el primer equipo no está asegurada. Una de las alternativas sería buscarle una salida a otra liga, especialmente a la Premier League, donde cuenta con numerosos equipos interesados. "Lo normal es que el Real Madrid lo fiche de vuelta y veremos si se queda en la primera plantilla o le da salida a otra liga como la Premier, donde tiene muchos equipos interesados", ha concluido Moretto.
