articles.title: Grading Top NHL Rookies 1 Month Into 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: It's not exam season at school yet, but we're pulling out the red pen for the top rookies in the NHL. One month into the season, we're seeing how their starts stack up against one another and where they might go from here.
articles.body:
It's not exam season at school yet, but we're pulling out the red pen for the top rookies in the NHL. One month into the season, we're seeing how their starts stack up against one another and where they might go from here.

Sometimes a rookie takes a while to find his feet, whether this plays out as a hot start that cools off, a slow start that trends upward, or an inconsistent run of games as he adjusts to playing in the big leagues.

You could lump players like Anton Frondell and Roman Kantserov of the Chicago Blackhawks, as well as Ilya Protas of the Washington Capitals, under this label. Frondell had an impressive start, though his pure scoring has not continued; Kantserov didn't score in his first five games, but has started to pick it up. As a group, they're a pretty good example of the range of rookie experiences.

We'll likely be folding these three into our grading in future updates, so keep an eye out. For now, let's turn our grading scale first to Boston and a former projected first-overall pick who went seventh.

Bruins forward James Hagens is currently tied with two others for second in rookie scoring, with 9 points in 13 games (4 goals, 5 assists). His point-per-game pace is also good for second in rookie scoring, at 0.69 points per game. That's all well and good, but the impressive part comes in when we look closer and see that 8 of those points are even-strength points. All of his goals have come at even strength. He's not feasting on special teams opportunities, but grinding away every minute he's out on the ice; it bodes well for how he's adjusting to playing in the NHL full-time.

It's not surprising to hear from those familiar with his play, particularly those who have watched him for a good long while, but it's a better start than probably many expected. He's 5'11"; he's still weedy at 180 pounds, but he's consistently throwing himself into the dirty areas of the play. We've seen him as a play driver, a highlight-reel goal scorer, someone who processes the game at such a high rate.

It's that processing that helped him realize that he can't rely on those fancy goals or sticking to the perimeter, and once he clocked that, he started driving to the net more and getting inside more. That adaptability is going to serve him very well, and because of that, the rest will come.

Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, RW, Detroit Red Wings

Winger Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has had a solid start on a team that is, to put it mildly, in turmoil. He currently sits fifth in rookie scoring, with 8 points (2 goals, 6 assists) in 12 games; his point-per-game pace at 0.67 is better than that of one of the three players tied for second. Brandsegg-Nygård is also averaging about 15:33 per game; the only players on this list with higher average playing times are Cole Hutson and Ivar Stenberg. He's really being relied on, and that seems like it's not going to change any time soon.

If he continues on his current trajectory, he could end up a dark horse for one of the Calder nominee spots. Obviously, we want to see how his play bears out over more games before we make that call, but it's never too early to note his potential. He's one of the few Red Wings players consistently bringing physicality and pairing it with offensive production, something the team seems to value.

He's got a bit of a leg up on other rookies who didn't have the time in the league he did last season; between that familiarity and being trusted on the second power-play unit, it's not a stretch to think he could stay on his current path.

This isn't the start that we wanted to see from Alberts Šmits, but part of that is the team itself. It's no surprise that the New York Rangers of late are not precisely a friendly environment for young, newly developing players. But it says a lot about the perception of Smits that not only is head coach Mike Sullivan praising him even as he is still searching for his first point, but he is also the first 18-year-old defenseman to play for the Rangers since Dave Maloney 52 years ago.

Smits is an incredibly intelligent details guy. He processes the game at a very high level, and that is only going to help him improve his game from here. Making decisions confidently is part of why the mistakes he's making—because he is—haven't been damaging him as much; the mistakes are less costly because of his lack of hesitation.

With all of this in mind, he's not really being deployed in an ideal way. He's struggling with his current defense partner, Braden Schneider; it would be interesting to see how he does with someone else over an extended period. He's not getting overwhelmed or drowning in his struggles, though, and that bodes well for him adjusting and finding his way through. But the Rangers also can't count on that; they need to utilize him better instead of just saying Oh, he'll be fine, and carrying on.

Winners and Losers From NHL's 1st Month 📊

Which Teams Are Pretenders or Contenders? 🤔

What is going on in Philadelphia? It's very odd that Porter Martone, of all people, only has 6 points in 15 games and is averaging about 14 minutes per game . Last season they were playing him at around 17 minutes per game, and his overall play looked better; maybe there's a lesson to be learned here. Why wouldn't you play such a highly skilled rookie more when your team is doing so poorly? Martone is ostensibly on the "second line", but his playing time doesn't reflect that.

To be clear: it is, of course, on Martone to find a way to make the minutes that he does play count. This is not all on the Flyers. Utilizing the opportunity in front of you as efficiently as possible is the only path forward in a situation like this. He's been a bit too passive along the boards, and there have been moments where he's lacked urgency; things we called him out for in his draft season that we hoped were shaping up are showing up here and there. His skating suffers when his pace is lacking.

With all that said, the team really needs to put him out there more. The only way out is through, and some players need more time to find consistency. With Martone, taking that chance will be worth it.

The only reason this is not a solid A-grade is that we'd really like to see more production from Ivar Stenberg at even strength. Right now he's feasting on the power play—and you know what, good for him. But he's a highly skilled player, and he absolutely has the talent to score at even strength.

Stenberg is one of three players tied for second in rookie scoring with 9 points; unlike the other two, his split is 3 goals and 6 assists. His point-per-game pace is tied with Hagens at 0.69, good for second among rookies. He's a great example of why we don't use plus-minus as an overall judgment metric, because he's a -9 right now, and that's not really reflective of how he's played so far this season.

So far, 7 of his points have come on the power play, as noted above. It's great that he's being trusted with that top power-play unit time, and it's something that we both hope and expect to see continue. He has been particularly good at identifying and taking high-danger chances, which is not surprising to anyone who has watched him prior to this season.

Hopefully, next time we grade these guys, more of Stenberg's points will be 5-on-5.

To absolutely no one's surprise, first-overall pick Gavin McKenna is leading all rookies in points with 11 in 15 games at the time of writing. His points-per-game pace is also the highest, at 0.73, and his points are almost evenly split between special teams and even strength, with 5 power-play points and 6 at even strength.

Although his average playing time is being dragged down by that Buffalo Sabres game where Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller only played McKenna 6:36 of the entire game, an average ice time of 13:46 is a little silly-feeling for a first-overall pick. Not really sure what that's about, unless it's a rookie load-management decision. That one would be a little easier to swallow. That should be going up pretty soon, though; McKenna just started playing with Auston Matthews on the top line due to Kirill Marchenko's recent injury and Marchenko being ruled week-to-week.

McKenna has had some struggles through the neutral zone and with some of his decision-making in general, but that was the kind of adjustment issue that we expected. We're really just looking for him to continue to grow that offensive contribution and find consistency; since we're only a month into the season, no alarm bells are ringing for anyone, especially not here.

Trevor Connelly, LW, Vegas Golden Knights

Vegas Golden Knights winger Trevor Connelly is tied for second in rookie scoring with Stenberg and Hagens at 9 points, but with a slightly lower point-per-game pace of 0.64, as he's played 14 games. His 4-goal, 5-assist split is the same as Hagens, and if he continues to play the way he has been so far this season, we fully anticipate him breaking the 20-goal mark. (It is also entirely possible he cools off and doesn't; it's still early.)

Regardless of his goal totals, Connelly has shown he has the ability to enter the Calder conversation. He's a highly skilled player whose on-ice discipline and decision-making have sometimes limited his offensive impact.

While a month isn't a long time, this start suggests Connelly is letting his skill lead the way. Another encouraging sign: He has no penalty minutes so far. For a player whose on-ice discipline has drawn criticism, that's a positive start.

If Connelly continues on his current trajectory, he'll be the first homegrown talent the Golden Knights have produced rather than traded away in at least six years. They have to feel good about that.

This is a B+ rather than slightly lower because, regardless of his production or any struggles or what have you, Cole Hutson has played 11 games at the time of writing, and Jack St. Ivany, who he played with Wednesday night, was his seventh defensive partner.

Yes, you read that right. His seventh in 11 games.

That's the kind of chaos even the Edmonton Oilers' coaching carousel of the early 2010s couldn't have dreamed up. So the fact that Hutson has five points, is averaging about 19 minutes per game (including four 20+ minute games that have dragged that average up), and the majority of his points are at even strength is going to impress us.

Ideally, the Capitals will find him a consistent defensive partner soon. It's really hard to judge the ins and outs of his game when he's playing with someone new every night. Hutson is such a special, skilled player, aggressive on offense and perceptive all over the ice. He'll be able to utilize that much more effectively if he has a consistent partner who can keep up and learn to read him.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Most Likely 1st-Time Champions After Brewers World Series Win
articles.summary: The 2026 World Series promised a new champion, with the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays both hunting for their first title in franchise history. The Brewers came out on top with a closeout victory in Game 5 on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
The 2026 World Series promised a new champion, with the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays both hunting for their first title in franchise history. The Brewers came out on top with a closeout victory in Game 5 on Wednesday night.

Which major sports team will be next to claim its first championship?

Across MLB, NBA, NFL and NHL, 36 teams have yet to win a title. While there is no end in sight to the drought for some of those organizations, others might be on the cusp of that long-awaited victory parade.

Ahead, we've highlighted the 10 most likely first-time champions now that the Brewers have officially exited the conversation.

Other Teams Still Chasing Their 1st Title

Brooklyn Nets Charlotte Hornets Los Angeles Clippers Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans Orlando Magic Phoenix Suns Utah Jazz

Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers Cleveland Browns Houston Texans Los Angeles Chargers Tennessee Titans

Buffalo Sabres Columbus Blue Jackets Nashville Predators Ottawa Senators San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken Utah Mammoth Vancouver Canucks Winnipeg Jets

First Season: 1976-77 NBA Finals Appearances: 2 (2000, 2025)

The development of Tyrese Haliburton into an All-NBA point guard and the addition of All-Star Pascal Siakam helped the Indiana Pacers make a surprise run to the 2025 NBA Finals.

They ultimately fell to the Oklahoma City Thunder in seven games, but the more crushing blow came in the fourth quarter of Game 7 when Haliburton suffered a torn ACL that would sideline him for the entire 2025-26 season.

The 26-year-old has returned to action this season, though he is now dealing with a hamstring issue. Once healthy, the pieces remain in place for the Pacers to return to their 2024-25 form and surge back from last year's 19-63 finish.

Reggie Miller never reached the mountaintop, but Haliburton still has a chance to etch his place in franchise history by delivering the organization's first title as the face of the franchise.

First Season: 1977 World Series Appearances: 0

The Seattle Mariners were eight outs away from reaching their first World Series during the 2025 ALCS when Toronto Blue Jays slugger George Springer hit a go-ahead three-run home run in a 4-3 Blue Jays victory.

With a stacked starting rotation, deep bullpen and offensive stars in Cal Raleigh, Julio Rodríguez and Randy Arozarena, they looked more than capable of making another deep October run entering the 2026 season, but instead stumbled to a 76-86 record.

Despite that disappointing finish, there are still few teams that boast their stable of pitching talent, with Logan Gilbert, Bryan Woo, George Kirby, Bryce Miller and Emerson Hancock making up a fully homegrown rotation.

After a 20-year playoff drought, they have made the postseason twice in the last five years. With a deep farm system and money to spend, this still feels like a team on the rise rather than one that missed a fleeting opportunity.

Way-Too-Early 2027 MLB Playoff Predictions 🔮

First Season: 1968 Super Bowl Appearances: 3 (1981, 1988, 2021)

The Cincinnati Bengals have the biggest box checked in the Super Bowl contention discussion with one of the league's best quarterbacks in Joe Burrow. He has already played on the biggest stage in 2021.

At 29 years old, he is in the prime of his career. He currently leads the NFL in completion percentage (71.7) while logging 15 touchdown passes against just three interceptions. With Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown, the Bengals have one of the best offenses in football.

Despite missing the postseason the last three years, this team still feels capable of Super Bowl contention. A convincing 35-13 road win over the Baltimore Ravens last week backs that up.

If their defensive improvement (28.9 to 20.3 points allowed per game) proves sustainable, they look like a legitimate threat to return to the AFC Championship Game. Burrow is one of the few quarterbacks good enough to put a team on his shoulders.

First Season: 1995 Super Bowl Appearances: 0

The Jacksonville Jaguars went 13-4 last season en route to their second AFC South title in four years. While they were bumped by the Buffalo Bills in the Wild Card Round, the season was still a massive success coming off a 4-13 finish the year before.

The foundation of their success last season was the NFL's stingiest run defense, allowing just 85.6 yards per game on the ground. They sit atop that leaderboard again, allowing just 72.2 yards per contest through six games.

Meanwhile, quarterback Trevor Lawrence is enjoying the best season of his career, with personal-best marks in touchdown percentage (7.6%), yards per attempt (8.0) and passer rating (106.2).

Anchored by their defense and a quarterback who looks to be on the doorstep of taking the next step in his career, the Jaguars have seemingly gone from afterthought to legitimate title contender in just two short years.

First Season: 1961 Super Bowl Appearances: 4 (1969, 1973, 1974, 1976)

The NFL's last remaining undefeated team this season, with a 6-0 start, is the Minnesota Vikings. They belong squarely in the first-timer discussion as they celebrate the 50th anniversary of their last Super Bowl appearance.

Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has built the league's most dominant scoring defense, allowing 12.3 points per game, highlighted by a signature victory over the Chicago Bears in Week 2, when they surrendered a lone field goal after the reigning NFC North champs piled up 59 points in Week 1.

The question is whether that defense can prop up one of the league's worst offenses all season. The offense has recorded just nine touchdowns through six games. Kyler Murray has not benefited as much as hoped from his offseason change of scenery.

All of that to say, defenses have carried teams to Super Bowl titles in the past. This is an awfully good Minnesota defense. The full picture of just how good this team is will take shape during their upcoming stretch of games against the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers.

First Season: 1998 World Series Appearances: 3 (2008, 2020, 2026)

The Tampa Bay Rays will likely need to replace Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez in the starting rotation, but aside from those departures, they will be running back essentially the same roster that just won 98 games and the AL pennant.

Few organizations do a better job finding value on the margins and maximizing every dollar they spend. The one-year, $13 million deal they gave Martinez in free agency is the perfect example of how they operate.

Buy low, maximize value and then let someone else pay for a standout season before moving on to the next potential source of value to continue contending on a shoestring budget.

With a bona fide face of the franchise in Junior Caminero, a pitching factory that helps guys level up time and time again, and a deep farm system, this is an organization built for sustainable success.

First Season: 1930 Super Bowl Appearances: 0

Two years removed from a 15-2 season that ended with a disappointing Divisional Round loss to the Washington Commanders, the Detroit Lions again have one of the most dynamic offenses in football.

Quarterback Jared Goff leads the NFL in passer rating (112.5), averaging 298 passing yards per game and throwing 14 touchdowns without an interception during the team's 4-2 start. He has established himself as one of the league's elite signal callers.

A potential statement game awaits on Sunday with a showdown against the Minnesota Vikings' No. 1 defense. They lost both head-to-head meetings last year.

An improved secondary looks like the missing piece to the Super Bowl puzzle. With Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Aidan Hutchinson and Penei Sewell in place as foundational pieces alongside Goff, the roster feels extremely close to Super Bowl-caliber.

First Season: 2000-01 Stanley Cup Final Appearances: 0

It's shocking at the surface level that the professional team in a state known for its love of hockey has never even reached the Stanley Cup Final, let alone won a championship, but that could soon change.

The Minnesota Wild have a face-of-the-franchise talent in winger Kirill Kaprizov. With 14 goals and 23 points through the team's first 14 games, he is on his way to a career year in his age-29 campaign.

Joined by elite defenseman Quinn Hughes and rising young goaltender Jesper Wallstedt, the roster has some legitimate pillars to build around. With a 9-3-2 record so far this year, they sit atop the Central Division standings.

After a first-round playoff exit in 2025 and a second-round loss in 2026, this group looks poised to take another step forward in pursuit of a long-awaited Stanley Cup.

First Season: 1989-90 NBA Finals Appearances: 0

The case here has to be prefaced by recognizing that Anthony Edwards is expected to miss the next two months after undergoing an arthroscopic cleanup of his knee, but that does little to take the shine off the Minnesota Timberwolves' future outlook.

After back-to-back trips to the conference finals, followed by a loss in the semifinals last season, the T-Wolves have firmly established themselves as one of the top-tier contenders in the Western Conference.

Still only 25 years old, Edwards is a championship-level superstar entering the prime of his career. For the four-time All-Star, a cleanup procedure reads as far better news than a meniscus issue.

Flanked by defensive stalwart Rudy Gobert and complementary pieces like Jaden McDaniels, LaMelo Ball, Terrence Shannon Jr. and Ayo Dosunmu, this is a dangerous team that has already experienced postseason success and potentially not yet reached its peak.

First Season: 1960 Super Bowl Appearances: 4 (1990, 1991, 1992, 1993)

There is already a strong case to be made that Josh Allen is one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history to not win a Super Bowl ring. Unlike Dan Marino and some of the other retired legends often mentioned in that conversation, he still has plenty of time.

With seven straight 10-win seasons, the Buffalo Bills have consistently been in the postseason mix throughout Allen's time as the starting quarterback. He has finished in the top five in MVP voting five times while taking home the hardware in 2024.

It takes more than a good quarterback to win a Super Bowl, but the Bills are off to a 5-1 start despite allowing 28.5 points per game, so even marginal improvement around their high-powered offense might be enough to make them a title contender.

As long as Allen is producing at an MVP-caliber level, the Bills will be a serious threat to erase the decades of heartbreak dating back to that four-year run in the early 1990s when they came up empty.

articles.title: Predicting What WWE Gains and Loses as Shawn Michaels Reportedly Replaces Bruce Prichard
articles.summary: Bruce Prichard is set to leave his position next spring, with a WWE Hall of Famer reportedly in line to replace him.
articles.body:
Bruce Prichard is set to leave his position next spring, with a WWE Hall of Famer reportedly in line to replace him.

Earlier this week, the news broke that Prichard requires neck surgery linked to an injury he sustained in 1991. According to Mike Johnson of PWInsider , he is expected to retire from his full-time role as Executive Director - Creative Writing & Talent after WrestleMania 43.

This is a huge development as Prichard has been with World Wrestling Entertainment for over 25 years. Most notably, he acted as a writer, producer, and Vince McMahon's right-hand man before his release in 2008. The 63-year-old rejoined the creative team as an executive in 2019.

Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select reported that he would remain with the company as a consultant, but he would work from home when the time comes. WWE is reportedly grooming Shawn Michaels to take on his role.

Given his connection to Triple H, this makes perfect sense. More to the point, HBK has been a writer and producer for NXT and a driving force behind the latest crop of young wrestlers.

This would be a major change, but it could be the move WWE needs to reshape the company in 2027.

A Much-Needed Change of the Guard for WWE

Obviously, this is interesting because Prichard is one of the last links to the McMahon regime. The former chairman and CEO still has a lasting imprint on WWE, but we're getting closer to a creative team built entirely by Triple H.

That's uncharted territory for the globally recognized purveyor of sports entertainment. However, the company desperately needs some new voices and fresh ideas. Promoting Michaels may not be the most drastic internal shift, but it's a step in the right direction.

Similarly, NXT could use a new approach, and AJ Styles has already surfaced as a potential replacement. The developmental brand has undeniably produced a wave of budding stars, but the weekly product has been lackluster.

Nevertheless, HBK excels as a coach, and his evident relationships with the wrestlers would make him an exciting addition to the current creative team. He may not have Prichard's years of experience, but he's the right man to usher in the next generation of Superstars.

WWE has already improved the pipeline from NXT, but this also ensures this era's call-ups will be handled with even more care. While Triple H is the public face, Michaels is more accessible and hands-on with the talent. The possibility of the two working closely together on the main roster is an intriguing move for the company's future.

Conversely, there are certainly some concerns about promoting someone so closely linked to Triple H and the McMahon family. It would be ideal to introduce someone entirely new, with an untainted vision for the product.

With all things considered, that was a highly unlikely outcome. WWE will promote someone trusted to steer the ship without changing too much of its time-tested formula.

That would make Michaels a strong candidate, and the benefits outweigh the drawbacks of his ascension. He has earned his peers' and the new talent's esteem and demonstrated an immense respect for the business.

Most fans will also approve of his promotion because they already know him as a legendary performer and promising off-screen presence. It may be a safe pick, but that doesn't mean it's not the right one for this regime. This seemed inevitable, but there's plenty of reasons to be excited about it.

articles.title: Ranking Halloween Havoc's 10 Greatest (and Weirdest) Moments in WWE NXT and WCW History
articles.summary: For the first time ever, Halloween Havoc will air as a premium live event for WWE NXT on Halloween night this Saturday, live from WWE's Performance Center in Orlando.
articles.body:
For the first time ever, Halloween Havoc will air as a premium live event for WWE NXT on Halloween night this Saturday, live from WWE's Performance Center in Orlando.

The concept was revived by the black-and-gold brand as an annual staple starting in 2020 and has been one of their most entertaining shows of the year since then. Prior to that point, Halloween Havoc served as a tentpole pay-per-view for WCW between 1989 and 2000.

NXT has kept the core spirit of the event alive by incorporating as many stipulations, spooky elements and colorful characters as possible. It's traditionally the one night of the year where the wrestlers are allowed to let loose and embrace the sheer madness of the haunted holiday.

There's been some standout matches and memorable moments at the October classic under the NXT umbrella, but very little has been able to come close to the craziness that ensued at the event during its days as an WCW exclusive.

From notable debuts and returns to career-altering performances and wacky gimmicks, these are the 10 greatest—as well as the weirdest—moments in Halloween Havoc history.

NXT 2.0 was still in its infancy at the time of Halloween Havoc 2021, which was largely built around the newer names that just debuted on the brand. The night saw Bron Breakker narrowly fall short of dethroning Tommaso Ciampa for the NXT Championship and Toxic Attraction assume total control of the women's division by taking all the titles.

Breakker wouldn't win the NXT Championship until a few months later and Toxic Attraction's success was eventually overshadowed by the dominance of Fatal Influence, but one moment from the event that did stand the test of time was Solo Sikoa's debut.

LA Knight and Grayson Waller were too busy beefing over who the rightful host of Halloween Havoc was when Sikoa, whose arrival had been hyped up in vignettes in the weeks leading up to it, emerged to make an immediate impact. He proceeded to take out both men in impressive fashion, establishing himself as a one-man wrecking crew in the process.

Sikoa has undergone quite the transformation as a character over the last five years, but everything he's accomplished can be traced back to that destructive debut.

9. Roddy Piper Confronts Hulk Hogan (1996)

The New World Order was mere months into their hostile takeover of WCW when Halloween Havoc 1996 rolled around, an event headlined by "Hollywood" Hulk Hogan successfully defending his WCW World Heavyweight Championship against Randy Savage in a heavily-touted WrestleMania rematch.

With Savage being the one Hogan betrayed when he turned heel at Bash at the Beach, all signs pointed to him being Hogan's ultimate opponent at Starrcade at the end of the year. WCW going with that match at Halloween Havoc instead left Hogan without an obvious adversary for the their biggest show on the calendar.

Hot Rod was fresh off a run as an on-screen authority figure in WWE, so it was certainly shocking to see him jump ship to WCW at a time when they were picking up steam. He walked out in the closing moments of Halloween Havoc to send the message to Hogan that he had another ghost from his past that he had yet to conquer.

Piper was treated like a massive babyface by the crowd that night, and his first-ever appearance for the promotion set the stage for a blockbuster Starrcade main event.

8. Tatum Paxley Wins the NXT Women's Championship (2025)

In many ways, it never felt like Tatum Paxley was intentionally put in positions to thrive in NXT. Rather, she was always an afterthought with very little direction but managed to capture the hearts and minds of the NXT faithful, anyway.

Her descent into darkness in 2024, specifically the storyline where she served as a stalker for Lyra Valkyria, was what initially helped her stand out. From there, she gradually gained momentum before finally becoming the breakout star of The Culling in the fall of 2025.

Fans didn't want to boo her despite The Culling being a heel faction, which made her the babyface by default in her NXT Women's Championship clash with Jacy Jane at Halloween Havoc 2025. Jane had reigned as champion for several months and didn't appear to be on the verge of losing the title anytime soon.

Once The Culling and Fatal Influence canceled each other out at ringside, Izzi Dame entered the ring and nearly blasted Jane with the NXT Women's title. That was enough of a distraction to earn Paxley the victory and her first-ever taste of gold on the brand.

Paxley's reign ended up being short-lived, but she did go on to hold the NXT Women's North American Championship as well as get called up to SmackDown this past summer.

7. The Chamber of Horrors Catastrophe (1991)

There a handful of stipulations that have only ever been done once because they were colossal failures, and WCW's Chamber of Horrors match from 1991's Halloween Havoc finds itself on that infamous list.

This was at a time when WCW could still be extremely campy and was trying just about anything to see what would stick. The innovation was appreciated, but the execution in this case left a lot to be desired.

Sting, El Gigante and The Steiner Brothers battled Abdullah the Butcher, Cactus Jack, Big Van Vader and The Diamond Studd inside of a steel cage. The catch was that you had to strap your opponent into a chair and "electrocute" them in order to win.

It was as silly as it sounds, though they attempted to make it work with some solid wrestling. It was weapons galore and just a total mess on the whole.

Abdullah was strapped down in the chair when Jack pulled the lever, accidentally awarding the babyfaces the victory. It was surely a sight to behold and somehow the perfect kind of catastrophe for a show such as Halloween Havoc.

6. Becky Lynch Passes the Torch to Lyra Valkyria (2023)

Becky Lynch's brief run as NXT Women's champion was one of the best things to happen on the brand in 2023, as it was completely unexpected and extremely beneficial for everyone involved.

The title reign gave Lynch something substantial to sink her teeth into and the opportunity for her to work with a bunch of fresh faces. Those fresh faces included Tiffany Stratton, Xia Li, Tegan Nox and Indi Hartwell, and all of them gained something simply from sharing the squared circle with her.

Lynch's toughest test as champ came when she had to defend against her former protege Lyra Valkyria, who at that time was struggling to find her footing in NXT. The crowd had yet to rally behind her, but this was her chance to show what she could do and prove her worth as a star on the rise.

The two had a terrific matchup, filled with suspenseful nearfalls and smart psychology with both women knowing each other exceptionally well. In the end, Valkyria pulled out the shocking upset to clinch the prestigious prize for the first time in her career.

It was a wonderful passing-of-the-torch type of moment that not only cemented Valkyria as the new face of the division but also eventually led to them rekindling their rivalry over the Women's Intercontinental Championship on Raw a year and a half later.

5. Cactus Jack and Big Van Vader Fight to the Death (1993)

Long before he became Mankind in WWE, Cactus Jack originally ascended to super stardom by waging war with all of the top titans WCW had to offer, Big Van Vader being chief among them.

Jack and Vader battered each other in a series of sadistic matches throughout 1993, culminating in a Texas Death match at Halloween Havoc 1993. It was built up as such an attraction that it actually closed the show over the WCW International World Heavyweight Championship bout between Rick Rude and Ric Flair.

The stipulation was determined by the "Spin the Wheel, Make a Deal" gimmick that remains a fixture of NXT's Halloween Havoc event to this day. In addition to securing a pinfall or tap-out, either man then had to ensure that their opponent could not return to their feet for a count of 10.

Their adulterated hatred for each other resulted in a barbaric battle on the ramp, near the entrance and on the floor. The constant chair shots and all of the other brutal bumps they endured caused copious amounts of blood to be spilled by both men.

The finish was a tad underwhelming in comparison when Vader's manager Harley Race got involved and cost Jack the win by putting him down with a stun gun. Jack was the last man standing afterward when he connected with a devastating DDT on Race, and it was his valiant performance that was the true highlight.

4. Dexter Lumis Terrorizes Cameron Grimes (2020)

For a brand known for its awe-inspiring in-ring action, NXT and its identity suffered the most from the limitations put on it by the pandemic in 2020. The great matches didn't quite hit the same in a near-empty arena, but to their credit, they made the most of it with a few fun cinematic matchups.

There were no two people more perfect for pulling it off at that time than Cameron Grimes and Dexter Lumis.

Grimes was a goofy heel at his most entertaining when he was trying to avoid getting his comeuppance. Meanwhile, Lumis was a creepy character whose obsession with Grimes led to them having their big blow-off in a Haunted House of Terror match at Halloween Havoc.

Grimes was exceptional at being scared, making Lumis a fantastic foil for him. Inside the haunted house, Lumis forced him to endure fright after fright, including an army of zombies that followed him all the way back to the ring.

Lumis locked Grimes in a sleeper to score the win and put an end to one of the most bizarre matchups to ever transpire in NXT.

3. Diamond Dallas Page Rises to the Occasion (1998)

Goldberg wasn't widely known for having barn burners at the height of his popularity, but he was WCW's hottest hand in 1998 and needed to keep his momentum rolling by delivering in the main event of Halloween Havoc 1998.

He was put up against Diamond Dallas Page, a newcomer to the main event scene. Page had just won WarGames the month prior and didn't pose much of a threat to Goldberg on paper, but being the beloved underdog that he was, he rose to the occasion and made believers out of everyone watching that night.

During the course of their competitive contest, DDP evaded Goldberg's signature Spear at every turn and targeted his right shoulder. DDP nearly had the match won when he nailed a Diamond Cutter on Goldberg and had the crowd buying into the possibility of him doing the unthinkable.

Although Goldberg did retain the title, DDP didn't walk away a loser whatsoever. He looked like a top guy in defeat and even earned the respect of Goldberg afterward.

Amazingly, this matchup did get the main event nod over the atrocity that was Warrior vs. Hulk Hogan, but the pay-per-view ended early and cut to black for most viewers because of an overrun, so there were many fans who didn't see it in real time.

For as many remarkable moments that have been synonymous with Halloween Havoc since its inception, there's been almost an equal number of train wrecks, akin to 1991's Chamber of Horrors and 2020's Haunted House of Terror.

Halloween Havoc 1995 as a whole was wild. It kicked off with a monster truck battle between Hulk Hogan and The Giant on a roof that played into their WCW World Heavyweight Championship collision in the main event later that night.

The bout was nothing short of awful and the excessive amount of interference and shenanigans hardly helped. To make matters worse, Jimmy Hart betrayed Hogan by hitting the referee with the belt to get his client disqualified and join The Dungeon of Doom.

In the midst of the chaos, a man dressed as a mummy walked down the aisle, entered the fray and assisted The Giant in attacking Hogan. Needless to say, their double bearhug on Hogan wasn't the least bit damaging.

If anything, it turned what was supposed to be a serious angle into complete comedy. Even the commentators' call of Yeti's appearance was worth ridiculing, and just like that, Yeti's WCW career was over before it could even begin.

1. Rey Mysterio and Eddie Guerrero Steal the Show (1997)

Not only is Rey Mysterio vs. Eddie Guerrero one of the very best bouts in the history of Halloween Havoc, it was also incredibly crucial to the careers of both legendary luchadors.

Guerrero's WCW Cruiserweight Championship was on the line as well as Mysterio's mask, so something significant was happening regardless of who went over. They did an effective job of making their match as meaningful as possible in the weeks leading up to it, and when the lights were on bright at Halloween Havoc, they did not disappoint.

For nearly 15 minutes, they battled back and forth and never let up. They worked a consistently-frantic pace and pulled out various moves in their respective arsenals that weren't being done regularly on American television back then.

Mysterio and Guerrero produced an absolute masterclass in storytelling, complete with high-octane action and an invested crowd. Mysterio winning was the stamp of approval he needed to cement his spot on the roster and add to his growing legacy.

Having been revered and emulated by so many, this is undoubtedly the defining Halloween Havoc moment.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: England 98-18 Wales: England thrash Wales to begin Wheelchair World Cup defence
articles.summary: Rob Hawkins says England "were not playing to our standards" despite beginning their Wheelchair World Cup title defence with a commanding 98-18 win over Wales.
articles.body:
Rob Hawkins said England "were not playing to our standards" despite beginning their Wheelchair World Cup title defence with a commanding 98-18 win over Wales.

Two-time winners England scored 18 tries to Wales' three in Wollongong, with Hawkins banking 11 tries and four conversions for an individual tally of 52 points.

Nathan Collins scored four tries and made nine of 11 conversion attempts, with Joe Coyd, Jack Brown and Mason Billington the other try-scorers for England in a victory Hawkins hopes will be a "stepping stone" towards brighter performances.

"Today's performance was a decent start for the team," said Hawkins. "It wasn't the best match we could have played.

"We definitely felt like we were not playing to our standards, giving away silly errors and giving away points.

"We're building so we can peak at the right time. Today was a stepping stone really."

Wales kept pace with the world champions for the opening 20 minutes, with tries from Stuart Williams and Sid Ramsey cutting the deficit to 18-12.

However, England blew them away with 28 unanswered points for a 46-12 half-time lead before adding a further 10 tries in the second half.

Ramsey added a consolation score for Wales – his second of the match – in the 71st minute.

Elsewhere in Group A, Ireland broke their international points record as they thrashed the United States 110-10.

Ireland's 20-try haul, which included seven tries for Joseph Calcott and six for Cian Horgan, ensured they surpassed the 92 points they put past Scotland in last year's Celtic Cup.

England are next in action against the United States on 3 November (07:30 GMT), with Ireland playing Wales (05:00) earlier on the same day.

articles.title: Hatton caps first undefeated season with 35-9 Central-Florence thrashing
articles.summary: Oct. 30—CENTRAL HEIGHTS — Hatton cruised to its first undefeated regular season in school history with a 35-9 win over Central-Florence on Thursday. "This ju...
articles.body:
Oct. 30—CENTRAL HEIGHTS — Hatton cruised to its first undefeated regular season in school history with a 35-9 win over Central-Florence on Thursday.

"This just doesn't even feel real," Hatton coach Nikita Stover said. "It really doesn't."

With their starting quarterback Cade Parham out for the week, the Hornet running game racked up over 250 rushing yards and all five Hatton touchdowns.

The Hornet defense held Central to less than 200 yards of total offense for the game, while the offense pulled out to a 28-0 lead by halftime.

Central's lone touchdown came late in the fourth quarter when Hattom was already up 35-2.

"This is the most fun I've ever had playing a sport, honestly," Hatton senior Taegen Burleson said. "We're such a team. Obviously, winning's a factor, but us being so together as a team is what's contributed to our record."

It's been a historic year for the Hornets.

Not only did the Hornets finish a perfect regular season, but Hatton also secured its first region title in 26 years and locked down a home playoff game for the first time since 2002, against New Hope.

"I've been starting on varsity football since my ninth grade year," Burleson said. "It's been my dream to build this program up. I've known we always had a chance to do something like this."

Hatton has been on a tear all season, outscoring opponents 380-105.

After star running back Savarius Evans went out in Week 6, they still outscored teams 117-29.

The most points any team has scored on Hatton was 20 by Brooks in the first game of the season.

"Even after we lost our star player in Savarius, we still prevailed and went 10-0," Burleson said. "That means a lot to me."

Hatton started the game with three straight 11-yard rush touchdowns. Two from Taegen Burleson and another from Quenderius Bolding.

Bolding then rushed 21-yards for a touchdown to put Hatton up 28-0 at halftime.

With two minutes left in the third quarter, a missed snap sailed into Hatton's end zone to give Central-Florence a safety that cut the lead to 28-2.

In the third period, Hatton's Keyshawn Bowling scored on a six-yard rush. Then Central had a four-yard rushing touchdown to cap off scoring.

Next week, they'll start the Class 3A playoffs and have a chance to break a first-round curse that goes back to 2002.

The Hornets have made the postseason nine seasons since then, including the last six years straight, but fell in the first round every time.

Last season they were within two points as they fell to Madison Academy 19-20.

"Losing that game p***** us off," Stover said. "So, we came back motivated."

"We're coming in hot," Burleson said. "We're going to make it happen."
authors: Zane Turner, The Decatur Daily, Ala.

articles.title: San Joaquin County flag football first-round playoff scores, recap
articles.summary: Of the 11 San Joaquin County flag football teams that entered Wednesday's first round, five advanced. Here's a recap of every game and its final score.
articles.body:
The road to a section championship is never predictable, and the opening round of the CIF Sac-Joaquin Section flag football playoffs proved it.

Eleven San Joaquin County teams entered the postseason Oct. 28. By the time the final games ended, only five were left standing.

Some teams took another step toward making history . Others watched promising seasons end before they could reach the quarterfinals.

Who survived the opening round? Which results turned heads? And how did the county's playoff field shrink so quickly?

Here's a closer look at every first-round result before the quarterfinals begin Monday, Nov. 2.

No. 6 Pleasant Grove 45, No. 11 Edison 0

The worst loss of Edison's season came at the worst possible time. After being shut out only once in the regular season, the Vikings were overwhelmed by Delta League runner-up Pleasant Grove, allowing their highest point total of the year.

What a difference a year makes. Last season, Tokay's playoff run ended with a 45-0 first-round loss. This time, the SJAA champions were on the other side of a shutout, scoring their most points since the season opener. Sophomore Asha Virk tossed five touchdowns, three to Yasmin Guadarrama, while Zoe Mirelez, Prabdeya Deol, Adison King and Isabella Martinez each grabbed an interception.

Sometimes the playoff draw just isn't in your favor. For Kimball, that meant facing Granite Bay, ranked No. 25 in California and No. 2 in the section. Still, sophomore Mackenzie Romeril, who had attempted just one pass all season, completed 12 of 17 for 100 yards and a touchdown to Yanelle Gill.

Everything seemed to favor Lodi. The county's best team during the regular season was playing at home, but Manteca spoiled the party. Lily Dundas completed 23 of 32 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns, with Gabby Leon hauling in eight catches for 162 yards and two scores. Myah Hayter contributed a touchdown and an interception, while Jaelyn Rosas made 16 flag pulls. Then came Sari Lawson's finishing touch, a walk-off interception to go with her touchdown and 10 flag pulls.

Tracy entered the playoffs as a TCAL co-champion with just five losses, and only fellow co-champion Lodi and Grant had managed to shut out the Bulldogs. That changed against Central California Athletic League champion Pitman, ranked No. 101 in California by MaxPreps.

A one-point try from Kayla Amarante ended up deciding everything. Even with Tessa Zalunardo held to her second-lowest passing total of the season, Sierra found a way to get it done. The quarterback, who entered with 3,912 passing yards and 53 total touchdowns, went 16 of 24 for 113 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions but remained effective on the ground with a team-high 77 yards on 11 carries. Freshman McKinley Robertson added an interception, while Amarante and Emalina Latu each scored.

Finding ways to win has become Lathrop's specialty. The Spartans entered the playoffs 20-3, having won three of four games decided by a single point, with Tracy handing them the only loss. This one wasn't quite as close, but it took a little help from the junior varsity team. Alexia Garcia, called up for the playoffs, completed 3 of 4 passes for 24 yards, including a 7-yard touchdown to fellow call-up Clarissa Garcia. Jaleiyah Ray contributed 65 rushing yards, 15 receiving yards and a one-point conversion, while Aaliyah Thompson's tackle for loss produced a safety.

Only one team had shut out Ripon all season, and it was the same team that held Tracy scoreless. Twelve Bridges, which finished third in the Foothill Valley League, became the second to do so.

No. 3 River Islands 48, No. 14 Leroy Greene Academy 0

On Oct. 23, 2025, River Islands walked off the field after an overtime loss ended its season at 8-10. The Riptide haven't lost since, improving to 19-0 and celebrating the program's first playoff victory. Ana Trigos completed 20 of 30 passes for 294 yards and accounted for five total touchdowns, while Sophia Delgado scored twice. Octavia Orndoff caught a touchdown among her 70 receiving yards, Kalina Rodriguez added 55 yards, a touchdown and her 26th interception, and Brianna Lee finished with 42 yards and a score.

Four years into its program, Millennium has yet to miss the playoffs. Unfortunately, that first postseason win will have to wait another year. Sonora entered at just 7-10 but showed why records can be misleading, scoring 50 points against a team that had allowed more than 20 only three times in its previous 16 games.

Hansi Flick spoke at a press conference ahead of the match against Alavés, as he looks to pick up all three points after last weekend's Clásico defeat.

He addressed several key topics, including Raphinha's call-up to Brazil's squad for the November international friendlies: "I've spoken with Deco and he's a very important player. After the last international break, he came back injured, which wasn't ideal. But it is what it is; we can't change it. I know Rapha is the captain here and holds the club close to his heart, but he's Brazilian and, when he's called up, he's ready. Every player wants to play for Brazil . If he can manage his playing time well, I'll be happy. Traveling to Singapore isn't ideal, but it's beyond my control."

At the press conference, the Barça coach also gave his view on the Ballon d'Or winner: "Kane deserved it. You know my opinion of Lamine ; he's good enough to win this award."

He left the door open to signing a defender in the upcoming transfer window: "I said it during the transfer window: we're always talking about what's best for the team and how we can improve it. That's something we're doing. We'll see. We still have a few weeks before the window opens. We've discussed it with Deco, Bojan and my staff. That's how we work. If we can, perhaps we will."

articles.title: Everything Luke Fickell said ahead of Iowa showdown
articles.summary: The Badgers head coach spoke to the media ahead of Week 9.
articles.body:
Fresh off a 24-7 win over the USC Trojans, the No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers are set to take on the Iowa Hawkeyes on Saturday in one of their biggest games of the season.

Wisconsin has been embarrassed in this matchup over the past two years, losing a combined 79-10, and is looking to avenge their loss and snap a four-game losing streak to the Hawkeyes.

Ahead of the game, head coach Luke Fickell spoke with the media, breaking down the matchup and all the important topics going into the game.

Here's everything Fickell said in his weekly presser ahead of Wisconsin's Week 9 game against Iowa.

Again, don't want to dwell upon the recap. I'm sure you'll ask some questions about it, but all in all, a great weekend, not just for us, but, I think, for a lot of things. I don't want to say Sunday was quite as good as Saturday night was with the Brewers and us both having big victories, but some really good things. To be honest with you, I was hoping for about 40 degrees, maybe a little rain, maybe light snow last Saturday, maybe thinking that guys coming in from Southern California would be a little bit better for us. Would we get 65, 68-degree weather and a perfect night? Then, the good thing was that we played well.

And so all's well that ends well, and it was a great weekend and a great night. But I didn't want to steal the thunder as the game ended and we celebrated, and those guys enjoyed the locker room to move forward onto next week. But I know for me, after about 4 or 5 minutes of finally finding a way off the field and saying hello to the family and things like that, my brain unfortunately started to move forward to, obviously, this week, rivalry week in particular. And so, I didn't want to take that from the players as they celebrated, and we enjoyed a little time there in the locker room. I told them to celebrate and enjoy, but I also left them with a little bit of that, hey, just remind yourself, remember this no arrogance or delusion, is really important, especially as we move ourselves forward to making sure we understand that, this next week what this thing brought to us.

And so, excited about rivalry week. It hasn't been great for us. And to be honest with you, you can point a few things at it, but I can tell you right off the bat here, I think we've been outrushed in this game over the last 3 years, like 740 to 350. I think that turnover margin in the last 3 years is 7 to 1. And so there's a lot of things that haven't gone well for us in this rivalry game. And we need to do a whole lot to change that. And it's not going to be easy. I don't know if there's a tougher place to play in the country, but that's what, that's why you go ahead and play this thing. And so for us, focus on ourselves too. I think we are getting better.

And I think that's probably the thing that leaves me awake at night as much as anything is, hey, are we consistently being good? Are we finding ways for us to grow and get better? And that's not just in one or two phases, that's in all that we're doing. And so it gives us another week to be able to do that, and so we're excited about that. I saw a bunch of guys trying to get the first question in there, so there must be some things that are hanging out there I don't even know about.

On changing the approach to rivalry games…

I think there's a balance there. Like, look, rivalries are still what makes college football, right? And we got to make sure we understand that this is a rivalry. This is the Heartland Trophy. Obviously it's been since 2004, but nonetheless it is. I think the big thing I didn't want to do was put too much emphasis on one in particular game as we went through spring football, as we went through fall camp, didn't mean I didn't want to focus on the rival. Didn't mean we didn't want to talk about the rival. Didn't mean we didn't want to understand who our opponents are going to be. But it did kind of say maybe there were some things that didn't, work out as well for us last year, putting a lot of emphasis, in the offseason, into the rivalry games in particular.

But I think it has a little bit more to do with us going into this week as much as anything, is, we got to be smart about the things that we're doing. We got to make sure we still continue to focus on us and how we're going to grow. Each and every week you have certain things you got to be able to do to have success in a football game, and sometimes each week's a little bit different. I can tell you this, stopping the run is still a critical part, and being able to run the football in every game is going to be critical. But I did stop trying to say, hey, let's take this offseason and spend a lot of time focusing on certain things, and as much as say, hey, let's focus on ourselves, we got a lot of new players, got a lot of new guys. We gotta really kind of enhance and develop this culture from within. And so we did probably spend a lot more time in that as opposed to studying and knowing, not that us coaches didn't, but as a program, in preparing for maybe this one or these couple rivalry games.

On Stylz Blackmon playing center and the offensive line facing Iowa…

I mean, I can't say that the last game wasn't a litmus test in seeing where the offensive line is, but I think there's a test, obviously, anytime you play Iowa, to say, okay, hey, you talk about being consistently good. Well, no one's been consistently good better, right? I don't know if that's even a word, good better, but longer, I should say than Iowa, and in particular, offensive line, defensive line. And so there is a test. There's a test every week. This is just a little bit of a unique, different test that we haven't done as well in.

So I think it gives us a better indication of some things and where we are. As far as Stylz, I think that, again, I think he's playing well. I think the thing about Stylz is we don't want to continue to move him around. I would love for him to get an opportunity to have some consistency at a position for longer than a week or 2 or 3. And, right now, I don't know exactly what that means just yet. I think he can play either position. I think it does have a little bit to do with where Austin [Kawecki] is and how comfortable Austin is as he comes back. And then trying to figure out what does give us the best opportunity to have our best 5 guys out there.

And so with Stylz having the versatility, with Stylz's ability to move around, that puts him in a position where we're going to ask a lot more out of him. And so I don't want to make him a master or a jack of all trades and a master of none, but nonetheless, I think that he has been able to handle it. And right now he'll probably have to continue to handle it for us.

On the run defense and Iowa's rushing attack…

Yeah, I don't want to put too much on our ability to have stopped the run so far because it's going to be a completely different challenge for us to be able to stop the run. But I think that we've always focused on, hey, can you play physical? Can you play really good down the middle to be able to stop the run? And so we've done a really good job. Those guys have done a great job so far this year.

And again, this is going to be a different test, not that one that you can't look back at and say, oh, pretty glaring when they've outrushed you in 3 years, 740 yards to 350 or 40-some yards, that we've got our work cut out for us. It'll be another great challenge. There are some things we got to do a little bit differently, but nonetheless, it still comes down to physicality. It's still coming down to controlling the line of scrimmage that we've done a really good job of so far this year. Like I said, sometimes stats don't tell the whole story. Last week it'll go down to -17 yards, which is what, the second-best since 1950 or something like that? And yes, there's a lot of negative yards played, sacks in particular, that help you with that. But I think it's been really good for us this year, but it's going to be a completely different challenge.

On Sebastian Cheeks' growth and leadership…

Yeah, I think for Sebastian in particular, I think one of the big jumps he made is, I think this past week. And it's not because, see, he had 2.5 sacks, or he had X amount of pressures and hurries. I think the big step that Sebastian made was Sebastian was dinged up for a bit of the week. Maybe guys didn't know it, but he was maybe a little bit questionable going into Tuesday, Wednesday practice. And so for Sebastian to make some of those steps of, hey, preparing himself, getting ready, maybe not being able to practice as much or do the things he wants to do on Tuesday and Wednesday, but to still be prepared and ready to play on Saturday, I think that was a big step for Sebastian.

I know he's an older guy, but sometimes that's not the easiest thing in the world for guys that haven't missed or haven't been out or haven't had some injuries. And so I think it told our guys a lot, his ability to prepare, his ability to maybe not be at his fullest on Tuesday and Wednesday, but yet still be able to go out there and perform. So I think, he's, he's shown those guys that, they have the utmost respect for him and how he goes about his business, that he'll be there on Saturdays. I think that's one of those big things that we do things in a certain way. Like I said, people talk about Posa and Catalano every single day, and Sebastian, like I said, he does it as well.

But when a time when you're a little bit dinged up, to show guys what kind of maturity you have and how you prepare and that you'll be ready on Saturday, I think that's a big step, especially as we push down this thing through the second half of the season.

No, I did not talk to him before the game. I don't know that I had some different conversation. I didn't want to make it bigger than it was, even though I knew it was big. And so for him, I wanted him to not think I was singling him out like, oh, like, oh God, we got to do something special here. W e got the utmost faith in him, hadn't had a ton of opportunities because of all the things that he's dealt with.

But nonetheless, I thought he did a really good job. I think that the moment wasn't too big, and we've said that in the past about a few guys, but when a guy's been out for as long as he has and it means so much to him, that's one of those things that sometimes you do worry a little bit about. Not that he's gonna turn anything down by any means, like the guy would lose an arm to be out there, but will he have the maturity and the control to be able to play the game the way the game needs to be played? And I thought he did a really good job.

We've kind of felt like Abu was going to be a guy that we were going to count on all year, from the time we got into spring football all the way through fall camp. And unfortunately, I think the first couple weeks he was healthy, hadn't been as healthy. And so this week, we felt like he was finally back to a spot where hopefully he could be healthier and maybe carry the ball, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, who knows, 17 times a game.

So it was finally that first probably opportunity that we actually had to feed him a little bit more. And sometimes they even come out of it saying, I wish we could have done it a few more times. But I feel like Abu's in a better place. I feel like he's getting more confidence in what it is he's doing, and it's not playing the game, but it's even in his health, that he is a little bit more aggressive in some of the things.

And so I thought it was a good start for him last week. It was a good balance there between him and B-Jack (Bryan Jackson) with DeeDee (Darrion Dupree) being a little bit dinged up. It's going to be a challenge for us to figure out who those guys are going to be. I know that Abu is going to be one of them, but, we should get DeeDee back and feeling more healthier, and B-Jack, who's proved a little bit more. So that entire room, there's a uniqueness of saying, hey, you love to play a lot of defensive linemen, right? And if they only play 15, 20, 25 snaps, that's good.

I think there's a thing with tailbacks that you got— it's harder to roll 3 guys in there. So the ability to say, hey, Abu's going to be, if he's your one, then he needs to get 60-65% of those reps. Who's the next piece? Who becomes the hot hand? And so I think that the offense in general has some work to do with that, but I think our guys have some work to do with that and as they prove things during the week.

I mean, we could go for quite a while here on not just the longevity of things, but their ability to not adapt what they don't have to adapt in the landscape of college football, that they've continued to do things in a cultural way that has been really impressive. Not to mention their play. I mean, nobody's been more consistent defensively, not just in statistical analysis of how they've played, but in the consistency of the way that they've played it since I studied them, I don't know, 25 years ago. They've made changes, but they haven't changed.

And they've adapted, but they've not changed. And so I know that's a uniqueness, they've always been a team that's going to focus on running the football, but they've grown and doing things differently as well. And so I think that, in a time of craziest amounts of change in college football, if there's one place that stands out more than any other in the country that has been able to do it in a consistent way, in the way that they know is best for them, is Iowa. And I've always had the utmost respect for what it is that they've done, and even more so over the last 4 or 5 years.

On transfer portal evaluation and additions…

We've, we've hit that in a lot of different ways. Obviously we know that each year has been unique, this year being a little bit different in the sense that we were looking for starters, and then you had to have resources in order to do that. And so that's why it was different. I think the numbers are still going to be, have been up there, a little bit higher than what you would want in the transfer world, to be honest with you, is the way we want to do things.

But it also comes down to when you're looking for guys in particular that you think have got to be starters, you had to have some resources. So the biggest difference this past year was what we were looking for in particular, like, man, we are going to need a heavy number of starters in the transfer world, to the resources that we had. It's not the way you want to live your life, I can promise you that, but it also has been what we had to be able to do.

And so, knock on wood, so far it's gone pretty well. We've created some depth that, through that world of not even knowing exactly what it is that you've got until you get into it. But that's not the way we want to continue.

On the sideline penalty involving Brady Collins…

Okay, so I don't know that I've ever not got a warning. I don't know that I've ever not— and I've only been a head coach for not a whole long time. I don't know, 10, 12 years, whatever it is. I've never not got a warning. Now, if I was an assistant coach, they would never have told me if there was a warning, probably. I guess you'd see the flag. I don't want to go all the way back to there, but no, I've never not gotten a warning for a sideline, and I don't think I've ever seen a personal foul called.

To be honest with you, I see it all the time. we just were clipping a few plays, not that I'm gonna send them, that they were like, hey, put that back. Oh, look, he ran into the official with no, with no flag of any sorts. I don't know. Did not send it in, haven't made any calls. It's just we've got to figure out the ways that we got to be better at the things that we do. But I would hope in the future that is not something that's in our game. I mean, whether it's for us or against us, like, that's not what we need. There's enough stuff going on the field. There's enough stuff that we're trying to all get better at and fixed. That's not one that we should be worrying about, you guys should have to worry about, and for sure shouldn't be called.

I don't know. I look, I just try to get myself out of there to go, get back to the team and things like that. I don't know what the rules are. I don't know if there's all the different fines of some sorts. Like, there's things that you can't stop. Like, I hate to say it's a part of college football, it's great about what the environments are in college sports in particular. Obviously there's a safety piece to this thing that we all got to be cognizant of, but I don't think it's malicious by any means. I think that shows college football hasn't changed, that there's some traditional things that make college football and college campuses so unique and so special.

On Cairo Skanes's development and versatility…

Cairo's another guy that, like I said, he's been able to play a lot of different things and do a lot of different things for us. He's the guy that, as you asked about the transfer world in the past, we were looking for guys that maybe had starting experience because you had some young guys— Cairo, Jai'mier Scott— that were guys that you felt really good about the future of them, just they hadn't played a ton.

And so Cairo's been a guy that has played multiple positions, started off at corner, played safety, 2 weeks ago got thrown in, and even this past week at nickel, where I don't even know if he took any reps during the week at. But he's a guy that the game isn't too big, the game isn't too fast. I still think he's just scratching the surface of what he is and what he's going to be, but he's a guy that is very valuable to us, and his name might not be mentioned or talked about as a starter, but in everything that we do, he's a guy that's a starter for us.

On building quarterback depth in the transfer portal era…

I don't know that the approach has changed, right? I mean, like, you want to have a room full of guys that you feel like the next starter, the next guy that can win in this league is in your room. It's just becoming and has been more difficult. It hasn't just been the transfer portal world. It hasn't just been the NIL world. That's been something to me over the last 10 years before the transfer portal started, before the NIL world started.

It was one of those things that you saw I think the top 30 quarterbacks in the nation, whoever you want to rank them by— Rivals, 247— I think when I did the study 2 years ago, I think over 75 percent of those kids had transferred from where they originally had gone to school. Whether that was— used to be the old grad transfer— whether that was early on when guys had to sit out, or this newer age where you don't have to sit out, I think over the last 10 years, it's been one of those things that's been more difficult. And I don't know that it's going to change, but it's something that I know every coach, obviously has a plan for.

But your plans have got to be able to adapt and adjust. And so, I feel like we're in a better place. I don't know about everybody else. A lot of times, as you've seen some of these guys that have left other places and gone and are having great success. There's a lot of really good players, quarterbacks in particular, out there that might not be starting. Hard part is you just don't know who they are and where they are. And so a lot of people need their opportunities, not a lot of people need their chances, and a lot of people are going to get them because of the nature of the game.

On Javan Robinson's impact on the defense…

I think anytime you got guys that you feel like are playing at or above their talent level gives you that opportunity. J-Rob's just been a guy for us, and to be honest with you, it's a great example of you don't know everything when you get a guy. And he was a guy that obviously had a lot of starts under his belt and had played good in his career. And to be honest with you, he's exceeded a lot of the things that maybe I even originally had thought of him, because sometimes as you see him walk in, you might think he's a little bit smaller, he's not quite as big, he's not. And he's everything but that.

And so he's doing a great job, and he showed us a lot this past week too because he'd been a guy that missed a little bit of time. He came out of the UCLA game, wasn't able to go a whole lot this week, but you— we got another look at what maturity looks like, what a pro playing the game looks like. And I don't mean just an NFL player, but a pro, meaning he can take care of the things he needs to take care of, whether he can get every rep, Tuesday and Wednesday or not.

But when Saturday comes, you can trust him. And not only can you trust him to go out there and play, but you can trust him to be honest with you to say, hey, I can do this. as opposed to, do you put the faith in a guy that you don't know as much about to say, can he really be prepared? Do we really want to put him out there? Because every play matters. But he continues to, I'd say surprise me, but he continues to impress me every day in all that he does.

On Junior Poyser and the defensive front…

That's where we knew coming into the season, I thought last year we were really strong. I didn't say we were great, but like we had, we had depth in that spot last year. We were able to roll guys. Guys were able to play 25, 30, 35 snaps tops. As we came into this year, we were missing a lot of those guys. And so as we brought Junior in, he was a guy that we felt like had good upside, had played in the MAC for really only a year. And so just kind of like, okay, how well is he going to transition? Is he gonna take an extra year?

As you look at Charles Perkins from last year, he didn't play much for us, and he's a completely different player this year. And as Junior came in, I'm not saying we didn't expect him to be able to play and play well for us, but you always wonder what that transition is going to be like. And I think he fit in pretty good initially, has played in every single game, and played a significant role. But I think you are starting to see him get a little better grasp of the level of ball, the way that which he has to play, and the confidence of which he can play with.

And so it has nothing to do with ability because he's got the size, he's got the strength, he's got the quickness to be able to do it. I think we're seeing Junior get more comfortable and confident in all that he does. And we're going to need him down the stretch, and in particular this week for sure.

On the defensive performance against USC…

Yeah, I think as much as anything, what it showed us is, and hopefully reminds our guys, that consistently good can win, and consistently good can win against really good talent. And I'm not saying that— not putting them down or saying anything different- but like sometimes you think that you gotta do some things differently. You gotta, you gotta do this you gotta blitz. I mean, like, I think the thing that our defense has done a really good job of, Coach Tressel and that entire staff and the players, that is they've recognized consistency. Right.

And their abilities to say each and every week, meaning, 2 weeks ago against UCLA, maybe the focus was a little bit more on stopping the run, and they'd had a tailback that had been leading— I'm not saying the Big Ten, if he was leading the Big Ten or is leading the Big Ten in rushing. And how you have to be able to play to a game— you go the next week against USC that's got a little bit more of a throw-it mentality, but you still have to be able to stop the run.

And understanding that consistency in what you do gives you the best chance to not only play well but be able to make adjustments as you get into game. And I thought that last week, as we got into the game, between the plan and the consistency, we were able to make some adjustments based on who they were and what they were doing. Because sometimes, until you actually see that kind of speed and that have to play in that kind of space that we don't play in every day, you got to be able to make some adjustments during the— during the game. And I think with the consistency, the ability to make those adjustments was where I think they've done a better job than they have over the last 3 years.

articles.title: Ilzer provides update on Conté after midweek injury setback
articles.summary: Bambasé Conté came on as a substitute but was forced off again as TSG Hoffenheim were eliminated from the DFB-Pokal by Holstein Kiel on penalties on Wednesda...
articles.body:
Bambasé Conté came on as a substitute but was forced off again as TSG Hoffenheim were eliminated from the DFB-Pokal by Holstein Kiel on penalties on Wednesday.

Having struggled with adductor problems ahead of the game, Conté started on the bench and was brought on after 64 minutes. However, he had to be substituted again shortly after the start of extra time.

"It was an issue against Lyon and in the games before that as well," Hoffenheim coach Christian Ilzer explained at a press conference on Friday, referring to last week's 3-0 win over Olympique Lyon, during which the attacking midfielder was forced off after 65 minutes.

A lengthy spell on the sidelines doesn't appear to be on the cards, but Hoffenheim will be determined to manage his workload to avoid aggravating the problem. Conté therefore looks unlikely to feature against Werder Bremen this weekend.

"It's an issue that requires a lot of caution to ensure it doesn't develop into a more serious injury," Ilzer said.

Another concern for Hoffenheim is Vladimir Coufal, who has been struggling with thigh pain for some time. The 34-year-old was initially rested in Kiel but had to come on after his replacement, Valentin Gendrey, suffered a broken fibula early in the match.

With Coufal's involvement also in serious doubt, 18-year-old prospect Natnael Abraha could make his Bundesliga debut at right-back against Werder Bremen.

articles.title: “Cracked me right in the nose”: Sophie Cunningham candidly recalls horrifying airport moment with Brittney Griner that gave her a black eye
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham once took a Louis Vuitton bag to the face at an airport, and she has now told the story.
articles.body: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham once took a Louis Vuitton bag to the face at an airport, and she has now told the story. She shared it on the This Past Weekend podcast with Theo Von. The bag belonged to Brittney Griner, her former Phoenix Mercury teammate, and Cunningham woke up with a black eye the next day.The same interview also covered a far more serious topic: how her rising profile has brought unwanted attention. Cunningham said the FBI is watching around 20 people over concerns they may be stalking her.How did Cunningham end up with a black eye at the airport?Sophie Cunningham and Brittney Griner were with the Mercury when a crowd swarmed the group in an airport. The team had no security, so the players formed a circle around the 6-foot-9 star. Griner was among the most talked-about athletes in sports at the time, after nearly 10 months in Russian custody before her release in December 2022.A man who appeared to be acting as security was carrying Griner’s Louis Vuitton bags. Cunningham was at the back of the group. She said he rushed in to clear the crowd and flung the bags aside, and one swung back into her nose. “I just get cracked by like a $5,000 bag,” she said.Cunningham laughs about it now. The league had far less travel support back then, and players often moved through airports and flew alongside regular passengers. She also used the moment to defend Griner, saying the Mercury veteran gets an unfair reputation and is easygoing and down to earth.Why does Cunningham say fame has a downside?Cunningham’s profile has grown a lot over the past year and a half, and she said not all of the attention is welcome. Stalkers are part of it. “I have, I think, 20 people that the FBI are watching for me alone,” she said. She called it a side of fame people rarely think about.She also credited the 2024 draft class for lifting the league. Caitlin Clark, Cameron Brink, Hailey Van Lith and Angel Reese arrived with a built-in college audience, Cunningham said, and the WNBA has grown fast since. Drafted 13th out of Missouri in 2019, she added that the league is now more diverse and is inspiring young girls to chase basketball careers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
